comment: 18 pages, 2 figures; includes supplementary material (S1-S11). Code and data: this https URL
summary: Image-conditioned video models are used to show real places, so whether their output stays faithful to the place they were shown is a practical question. The text benchmarks we found that check fidelity against a reference do so at an anchor - an annotated region, typically the sign the task is about. We show that this choice hides most of the failure. We conditioned four models from three vendors on 48 street-level references of Tokyo storefronts and measured text fidelity at the annotated sign and in the periphery, the other text the reference covers. At the anchor, all four models are close to a no-model control (anchor text fidelity 0.90-0.94 against 0.996) and are not reliably separated from one another. In the periphery, 36-54% of generated text regions have no counterpart in the reference, against 1.6% for the control, although every prompt forbade new readable text. Two blinded raters agree on which regions are fabricated (kappa = 0.83-0.96), the result held in preregistered rounds on two vendors whose videos the measure had never seen (42% and 56%), and VBench-I2V's reference-based consistency scores show no evidence of tracking it in our sample. Most fabricated text is legible-looking text where the reference shows none or cannot be read - a form that string-matching metrics discard, which is why our own first measure missed it. A preregistered Latin-script replication in London missed its bar in a first round and met it in an independent second round. We release code, annotations, per-video scores, ratings and every preregistration. Code and data: this https URL

AI.tldr: Anchor-based text fidelity benchmarks hide most text fabrication in image-conditioned video generation; measured in the periphery, 36-54% of generated text regions have no counterpart in the reference, against 1.6% for a control.
AI.motivation: Image-conditioned video models are used to show real places, but text fidelity benchmarks check only an annotated anchor region, which may hide failures elsewhere in the frame.
AI.method: Four models from three vendors are conditioned on 48 street-level Tokyo storefront references, and text fidelity is measured at the annotated sign and in the periphery, with blinded raters, preregistered rounds on two vendors and a Latin-script replication in London.
AI.result: At the anchor, all four models score 0.90-0.94 against 0.996 for a no-model control and are not reliably separated; in the periphery 36-54% of generated text regions have no counterpart in the reference, against 1.6% for the control, although every prompt forbade new readable text. Two raters agree on fabricated regions (kappa 0.83-0.96), the result held in preregistered rounds (42% and 56%), and the London replication met its bar in a second round.
AI.conclusion: Anchor-based evaluation misses most fabricated text, and string-matching metrics discard this legible-looking fabrication, so periphery-aware evaluation is needed; code, annotations, scores and preregistrations are released.

title: Sequential Transfer Learning for Plant Disease Recognition Across Perennial Crop Domains Using MobileNetV2-CBAM
summary: Purpose: This study investigates whether a learned disease-recognition representation can be progressively reused across distinct perennial crop domains and how its predictive behaviour changes as target-domain heterogeneity increases. Design/methodology/approach: A lightweight MobileNetV2 framework enhanced with the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) was evaluated through sequential transfer from Walnut to Cashew, Coffee and Mango, followed by validation on the heterogeneous ABCGMP six-crop benchmark. Each stage used the preceding model representation and was evaluated on an independent test set using complementary classification measures. Findings: Test accuracy increased from 75.76% for the Walnut baseline to 84.85% after CBAM integration, followed by 90.67% on Cashew, 100.00% on Coffee and 99.50% on Mango. The final ABCGMP evaluation achieved 88.44% accuracy, 81.49% Balanced Accuracy and 0.9949 ROC-AUC. The results show that substantial predictive capability was retained through successive crop transfers, while broader multi-crop heterogeneity introduced a measurable performance constraint. Originality: The study provides an empirical characterisation of sequential knowledge reuse across multiple perennial crop domains using a common lightweight attention-enhanced representation, extending evaluation beyond isolated source-to-target transfer.

AI.tldr: A MobileNetV2 with CBAM attention is transferred sequentially across perennial crop domains, from Walnut to Cashew, Coffee and Mango, reaching 88.44% accuracy on the heterogeneous six-crop ABCGMP benchmark.
AI.motivation: It is unknown whether a learned plant disease representation can be progressively reused across distinct perennial crop domains and how predictive behaviour changes as target heterogeneity increases.
AI.method: A lightweight MobileNetV2 enhanced with the Convolutional Block Attention Module is trained sequentially, with each stage using the preceding model's representation, from Walnut to Cashew, Coffee and Mango, then validated on the ABCGMP six-crop benchmark with complementary classification measures.
AI.result: Test accuracy rises from 75.76% for the Walnut baseline to 84.85% after CBAM, then 90.67% on Cashew, 100.00% on Coffee and 99.50% on Mango; the final ABCGMP evaluation achieves 88.44% accuracy, 81.49% balanced accuracy and 0.9949 ROC-AUC.
AI.conclusion: Substantial predictive capability is retained through successive crop transfers, while broader multi-crop heterogeneity introduces a measurable performance constraint.

title: AdaptAD: Foundation Model Adaptation with Missing Modality Robustness for Alzheimer's Disease Staging Across the Disease Continuum
summary: Staging Alzheimer's disease (AD) across its continuum, from cognitively normal (CN) through mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to dementia from a single structural MRI remains difficult because 3-D networks overfit small cohorts, and FreeSurfer morphometry is often unavailable. We present AdaptAD, which reads a registered T1-weighted scan as 16 anatomically placed 2.5-D slices through the medial temporal lobe and adapts a frozen ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), training 3.5 M of 89 M parameters. Morphometry enters as tokens when present, or as a learned [MISSING] token, and a missing-aware stacker fuses both experts. Under a pre-registered protocol, ten methods were compared for three-class CN/MCI/AD staging on identical 5-fold splits of 597 ADNI participants, 29% without FreeSurfer, with Holm-corrected paired bootstrap tests. The locked model was tested once on 993 OASIS-3 participants (988 scored by every method). On ADNI, AdaptAD achieved a three-class macro-AUC of 0.745 (95% CI 0.709 to 0.781), ranking first and significantly exceeding full fine-tuning, ShaSpec and a 3-D CNN. On OASIS-3 it reached 0.780 (0.748 to 0.814), and on the CDR-based label (0.804) it significantly outperformed every 3-D and image-tabular method. LoRA matched full fine-tuning with 25 times fewer trainable parameters, and removing morphometry changed external macro-AUC by less than 0.003. The disease score tracked MMSE and CDR-SB within diagnostic groups and stratified MCI-to-dementia progression (log-rank p < 0.001), while saliency concentrated in medial temporal and periventricular regions. A parameter-efficient 2-D foundation model can therefore stage the full AD continuum from a routine T1 scan without morphometry, offering a scalable route to memory-clinic deployment.

AI.tldr: AdaptAD adapts a frozen ViT-B/16 with LoRA to stage Alzheimer's disease (CN, MCI, AD) from a single T1 MRI using 2.5-D slices, achieving 0.745 macro-AUC on ADNI and 0.780 on OASIS-3 without requiring morphometry.
AI.motivation: Three-dimensional networks overfit small cohorts, and FreeSurfer morphometry is often unavailable, so staging across the full AD continuum from routine MRI remains difficult.
AI.method: A registered T1 scan is read as 16 anatomically placed 2.5-D slices through the medial temporal lobe; a frozen ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 is adapted with LoRA (3.5M of 89M parameters trainable); morphometry enters as tokens or a learned [MISSING] token, and a missing-aware stacker fuses experts, compared against ten methods under a pre-registered protocol.
AI.result: On ADNI (597 participants, 5-fold splits), AdaptAD reaches three-class macro-AUC 0.745 (95% CI 0.709 to 0.781), ranking first and significantly exceeding full fine-tuning, ShaSpec and a 3-D CNN; on OASIS-3 (993 participants, tested once) it reaches 0.780 (0.748 to 0.814), and 0.804 on the CDR-based label; LoRA matches full fine-tuning with 25 times fewer trainable parameters, and removing morphometry changes external macro-AUC by less than 0.003.
AI.conclusion: A parameter-efficient 2-D foundation model can stage the full AD continuum from a routine T1 scan without morphometry, offering a scalable route to memory-clinic deployment.

title: Rethinking Feature Perturbation for Single-Source Domain Generalization: A Representation-Space Analysis and Spectral Case Study
summary: Feature perturbation is widely used in single-source domain generalization (SSDG), yet it is typically evaluated by task performance rather than by the representation changes it induces. We investigate whether perturbations can be compared through measurable descriptors of these changes. We introduce a four-dimensional representation-space description comprising feature displacement $D_F$, relational displacement $D_R$, a task-region ratio $\Theta_{\mathrm{Task}}$, and subspace deviation $\Theta_{\mathrm{Subspace}}$. We use these descriptors as an empirical analysis framework, not as a universal geometry, to characterize existing perturbation mechanisms. Across two object-detection settings involving style and weather shifts, we observe distinct geometric profiles and a concentration of relatively strong out-of-domain (OOD) configurations within a bounded region of the descriptor space. These findings do not establish a universal optimum but motivate investigating whether regions associated with stronger SSDG performance can be identified without target-domain access. As a case study, we introduce Dual-Invariant Spectral Perturbation (DISP), a non-learned Fourier-phase perturbation with explicit controls over phase magnitude $\rho$, channel coupling $\kappa$, and frequency support $\mathcal{M}$. We empirically examine how these controls affect the proposed descriptors. DISP achieves strong OOD performance in our experiments, illustrating how explicit perturbation controls can be analyzed through a representation-space description. We hope this viewpoint can contribute to more interpretable, controllable, and ultimately testable approaches to feature perturbation in SSDG.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a four-dimensional representation-space description of feature perturbations for single-source domain generalization, and uses it to motivate DISP, a non-learned Fourier-phase perturbation with explicit controls that achieves strong OOD performance.
AI.motivation: Feature perturbations in single-source domain generalization are evaluated by task performance rather than by the representation changes they induce, so perturbations cannot be compared through measurable descriptors.
AI.method: Four descriptors are defined: feature displacement D_F, relational displacement D_R, a task-region ratio, and subspace deviation; DISP is a Fourier-phase perturbation with controls over phase magnitude, channel coupling and frequency support, analyzed as a case study on two object-detection settings with style and weather shifts.
AI.result: The descriptors reveal distinct geometric profiles for existing perturbations and a concentration of relatively strong OOD configurations in a bounded region of descriptor space; DISP achieves strong OOD performance in the experiments.
AI.conclusion: The authors present the descriptors as an empirical analysis framework rather than a universal geometry, and hope they support more interpretable and testable approaches to feature perturbation; the paper does not establish a universal optimum.

title: OCRia-1 Technical Report
summary: We introduce OCRia-1, a 4B vision-language model (VLM) for document parsing that excels at preserving table structure, extracting chart data and retaining text formatting. OCRia-1 handles content that has traditionally been challenging in document parsing: merged cells and spanning headers, tables with thousands of cells, chart data, and meaningful text formatting such as bold, italics, subscripts and superscripts, preserving details needed for business-critical document analysis. At the time of this report, it achieves the highest scores on tables, charts and text formatting among the systems evaluated, including a 35B model and Mistral OCR 4.1. Its mean ParseBench score over the four dimensions we evaluate is 0.87, against 0.75 for the next-best system. We emphasize data quality and reward design in training OCRia-1. Synthetic pages provide exact ground truth for long tables and rich formatting, while real pages are transcribed using a pipeline grounded in the PDF text layer. We attribute OCRia-1's performance primarily to careful data curation that prioritizes quality and diversity over quantity. Dimension-specific rewards evaluate table reconstruction, chart-data extraction and text-formatting fidelity. We train the model on the curated data using supervised fine-tuning (SFT), then refine it through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). To our knowledge, OCRia-1 is the fastest published document-parsing VLM in its class, decoding at about 4,700 tokens per second with a single request on one B200 GPU, about nine times faster than the base model on stock vLLM. This is achieved through a block-diffusion speculator, quantization and custom kernels.

AI.tldr: OCRia-1 is a 4B vision-language model for document parsing that preserves table structure, chart data and text formatting, reporting an average ParseBench score of 0.87 against 0.75 for the next-best system and decoding about nine times faster than its base model.
AI.motivation: Document parsing has struggled with merged cells, large tables, chart data and text formatting such as bold, italics, subscripts and superscripts, which matter for business-critical document analysis.
AI.method: Training uses curated synthetic pages with exact ground truth plus real pages transcribed through a pipeline grounded in the PDF text layer, supervised fine-tuning, then reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using dimension-specific rewards for tables, charts and text formatting; speed comes from a block-diffusion speculator, quantization and custom kernels.
AI.result: OCRia-1 achieves the highest scores on tables, charts and text formatting among the evaluated systems, including a 35B model and Mistral OCR 4.1, with a mean ParseBench score of 0.87 over four dimensions against 0.75 for the next-best system; it decodes at about 4,700 tokens per second on one B200 GPU, about nine times faster than the base model on stock vLLM.
AI.conclusion: Careful data curation prioritizing quality and diversity, together with dimension-specific rewards, is credited for the performance, and the model is presented as the fastest published document-parsing VLM in its class.

title: Pano2BIM: A Geometry-Constrained Vision-Language Agent for As-Built BIM Generation from a Floor Plan and a Single 360$^\circ$ Image
summary: Digital twins require accurate, up-to-date building information models (BIM) that reflect physical conditions, yet generating and maintaining as-built models remains costly and labor-intensive. Emerging image-based methods can capture visual appearance without inherently producing structured BIM information, while vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with reliable metric object placement. This paper presents Pano2BIM, a geometry-constrained VLM agent that generates approximate IFC4 models at Level of Development (LOD) 200 from a floor plan with known room dimensions and a single 360-degree photograph. The VLM identifies landmarks and objects, while deterministic tools estimate camera pose, compute metric positions through ray casting, and check spatial constraints. An optional second stage enriches the presentation model through render-and-compare feedback without modifying the primary furniture geometry. In a preliminary evaluation on one laboratory, the proposed Measure workflow achieved a mean furniture-footprint intersection over union (IoU) of 0.53, compared with 0.44 for a single-response baseline using identical modeling instructions, and matched an average of 4.0 versus 2.3 of seven fixed furniture elements across three runs. Centroid disagreements were similar for the four elements consistently identified by both approaches. The measurement stage averaged 3.8 minutes and USD 1.63 in API costs per run, while the complete demonstrated workflow required approximately 42 minutes and USD 11. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of rapid, low-cost as-built BIM generation, with potential applications in maintaining digital twins that reflect changing physical conditions.

AI.tldr: Pano2BIM is a geometry-constrained vision-language agent that generates approximate IFC4 as-built BIM models at LOD 200 from a floor plan and a single 360-degree photo, with a preliminary single-laboratory evaluation showing higher furniture-footprint IoU than a single-response baseline at low cost.
AI.motivation: Maintaining as-built building information models is costly and labor-intensive, and image-based methods do not produce structured BIM information, while VLMs struggle with reliable metric object placement.
AI.method: The VLM identifies landmarks and objects, while deterministic tools estimate camera pose, compute metric positions by ray casting and check spatial constraints; an optional second stage enriches the presentation model through render-and-compare feedback without modifying the primary furniture geometry.
AI.result: In a preliminary evaluation on one laboratory, the Measure workflow achieves a mean furniture-footprint IoU of 0.53 against 0.44 for a single-response baseline, and matches an average of 4.0 versus 2.3 of seven fixed furniture elements across three runs; the measurement stage averages 3.8 minutes and USD 1.63 per run, and the full workflow about 42 minutes and USD 11.
AI.conclusion: The findings demonstrate feasibility of rapid, low-cost as-built BIM generation, with potential for maintaining digital twins.

title: A Novel Lightweight Multi-Scale Branching Encoder for Few-Shot Image Classification
comment: Preprint version. This manuscript has not yet been submitted to a journal, IEEE Access, In press, pp.1-1
summary: Few-Shot Learning (FSL) addresses classification scenarios in which only a small number of labeled examples are available for each class. This paper presents the Sum12 Multi-Scale branching encoder, a lightweight convolutional architecture designed to improve the embedding stage of Prototypical Networks without substantially increasing computational cost. The encoder uses seven parallel convolutional branches whose kernel-size combinations sum to 12, allowing local and broader spatial structures to be represented within a unified Multi-Scale feature space. The proposed architecture was evaluated on Omniglot, CIFAR- FS, FC100, and miniImageNet under controlled few-shot learning protocols and compared with the original Prototypical Network encoder and Inception-inspired branch variants. Additional ablation studies have investigated fusion strategies, dilated convolutions, branch compositions, and receptive field budget. Beyond few-shot learning, the encoder was also tested on the MedMNIST 2D benchmark to assess its behavior in conventional supervised medical image classification. Across these experiments, Sum12 generally improved the low-shot classification performance with respect to the basic ProtoNet encoder while preserving a compact model size. These properties suggest that the proposed encoder may be suitable for low-data visual recognition and resource-constrained intelligent imaging applications. However, complete end-to- end validation on the target embedded platform, including resolution of the observed implementation discrepancies, remains future work.

AI.tldr: Sum12 is a lightweight multi-scale branching encoder for Prototypical Networks that uses seven parallel convolutional branches whose kernel sizes sum to 12, generally improving low-shot classification over the basic ProtoNet encoder while keeping model size compact.
AI.motivation: Few-shot learning needs embeddings that capture both local and broader spatial structure, and the ProtoNet encoder can be improved without substantially increasing computational cost.
AI.method: The Sum12 encoder uses seven parallel convolutional branches with kernel-size combinations summing to 12, fused into a unified multi-scale feature space; it is compared with the original ProtoNet encoder and Inception-inspired branch variants, with ablations on fusion, dilated convolutions, branch composition and receptive field budget.
AI.result: Evaluated on Omniglot, CIFAR-FS, FC100 and miniImageNet, Sum12 generally improves low-shot performance over the basic ProtoNet encoder while preserving compact model size; it was also tested on the MedMNIST 2D benchmark.
AI.conclusion: The encoder may suit low-data and resource-constrained imaging, but end-to-end validation on the target embedded platform, including resolving observed implementation discrepancies, remains future work.

title: Demystifying Prompt Stealing Attacks against Synthetic Video
summary: Creators publicly showcase generated content to advertise and sell their work, but these examples may also enable unauthorized reproduction and customization. We study whether an adversary can derive reusable inputs from a single public video for faithful reconstruction and controlled editing, without access to the original prompt or generator. We adapt captioning and prompt optimization approaches to video prompt stealing attacks (PSAs) and find that prompt recovery alone provides limited reconstruction fidelity. Even the original prompt produces different spatial and temporal realizations when the initial noise changes. Using an independent generator enlarges the reconstruction gap, as reusing the original prompt and seed can still produce substantially different videos. We propose V-PSA, which uses a recovered caption and DDIM inversion to construct a reference trajectory under an independent generator. Null-Text Inversion then optimizes per-step unconditional embeddings to reduce deviations from this trajectory during reconstruction. The resulting inputs also guide generation when the caption is modified, supporting edits that change selected content while preserving the target's layout and motion. We construct a benchmark containing 12,000 video-prompt pairs from three victim generators and four prompt sources. V-PSA achieves video-to-video similarity around 0.9 between target and reconstructed videos, substantially improving over prompt-only baselines with similarity score of 0.6, and supports multiple controlled variations that preserve the target's structure. Additional experiments show that augmenting prior image PSAs with inversion-derived inputs also improves reconstruction. Our results show that evaluations restricted to prompt recovery can underestimate an attacker's ability to reconstruct public generative outputs.

AI.tldr: V-PSA is a video prompt stealing attack that recovers a caption and uses DDIM inversion and Null-Text Inversion to reconstruct a public synthetic video with about 0.9 video similarity under an independent generator, versus about 0.6 for prompt-only baselines.
AI.motivation: Creators publicly showcase generated videos, which may enable unauthorized reproduction, but prompt recovery alone gives limited reconstruction fidelity because the same prompt and noise can produce different videos.
AI.method: V-PSA uses a recovered caption and DDIM inversion to build a reference trajectory under an independent generator, then applies Null-Text Inversion to optimize per-step unconditional embeddings that reduce deviation from this trajectory; a benchmark of 12,000 video-prompt pairs from three victim generators and four prompt sources is constructed.
AI.result: V-PSA achieves video-to-video similarity around 0.9 between target and reconstructed videos, against about 0.6 for prompt-only baselines, supports controlled edits that preserve layout and motion, and also improves prior image attacks when augmented with inversion-derived inputs.
AI.conclusion: Evaluations restricted to prompt recovery can underestimate an attacker's ability to reconstruct and edit public generative outputs.

title: Detector-Integrated Multi-Cue Association for Occlusion-Aware UAV Multi-Object Tracking
summary: Multi-object tracking (MOT) in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is challenging because vehicles are small, visually similar, and frequently occluded, which leads to identity switches (IDSW). Appearance-based trackers such as DeepSORT rely on a standalone re-identification (ReID) network, whose per-target inference limits runtime speed, while the appearance of small or occluded vehicles remains unreliable. This paper proposes a detector-integrated multi-cue tracking framework. Lightweight projection heads are attached to the neck of the YOLOv8n detector to extract target embeddings through ROIAlign, producing detections and embeddings in a single forward pass. A multi-cue association cost then combines motion, IoU, and appearance distances with weights determined through ablation, complemented by low-score rescue and appearance-memory protection. On the UAVDT benchmark, the proposed method achieves a MOTA of 28.33, a HOTA of 31.16, and an IDF1 of 38.18 at 82.59 FPS, the best among the compared trackers in all three metrics, and reduces IDSW by 58.4\% compared with DeepSORT.

AI.tldr: A detector-integrated tracker attaches lightweight embedding heads to YOLOv8n and combines motion, IoU and appearance cues to track vehicles in UAV video, reaching 82.59 FPS with the best MOTA, HOTA and IDF1 on UAVDT and 58.4% fewer identity switches than DeepSORT.
AI.motivation: Vehicles in UAV imagery are small, visually similar and often occluded, and DeepSORT's standalone ReID network limits runtime speed while its appearance cues are unreliable for small or occluded targets.
AI.method: Lightweight projection heads on the YOLOv8n neck extract embeddings via ROIAlign in a single forward pass, and a multi-cue association cost combines motion, IoU and appearance distances with ablation-determined weights, complemented by low-score rescue and appearance-memory protection.
AI.result: On UAVDT the method achieves MOTA 28.33, HOTA 31.16 and IDF1 38.18 at 82.59 FPS, the best among compared trackers on all three metrics, and reduces identity switches by 58.4% compared with DeepSORT.
AI.conclusion: Integrating embedding extraction into the detector gives a faster and more accurate UAV tracker than a separate ReID pipeline.

title: Dynamic Merging Mutually-Distilled Multi-View Networks for RGB-Event-based Representation Learning
summary: Multi-modal fusion algorithms combining conventional frame-based cameras and event cameras have recently attracted substantial research attention. Typically, existing approaches convert event streams into frames, voxels, or tensors, and then learn the required spatiotemporal information from these transformed event representations for fusion with conventional frame-camera data. Obviously, such paradigms only exploit the limited representational capacity of event data. Moreover, standard training pipelines fail to fully leverage diverse model parameters obtained throughout the learning process. In this paper, we propose a novel mutual distillation method leveraging multi-view teacher network weights to better integrate multiple event representations and achieve model-parameter level fusion. Specifically, we employ multiple encoders to extract different types of event representations and perform mutual knowledge distillation at both the feature-level and logit-level in this process. Afterwards, we perform a dynamic hierarchical model merge strategy on the model parameters from the first stage to yield a unified multi-modal RGB-Event representation model. Experimental results across multiple event-based datasets demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves significant performance improvements.

AI.tldr: A mutual distillation method for RGB-event fusion trains multiple encoders on different event representations, distills between them at feature and logit levels, then merges their parameters into one multi-modal model, reporting significant gains on event-based datasets.
AI.motivation: Event-camera methods convert event streams into frames, voxels or tensors that exploit only a limited part of event data, and standard training does not fully use the diverse parameters obtained during learning.
AI.method: Multiple encoders extract different event representations and perform mutual knowledge distillation at feature and logit levels; a dynamic hierarchical model merge then combines the first-stage parameters into one unified RGB-Event representation model.
AI.result: The abstract reports significant performance improvements across multiple event-based datasets, without giving specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Model-parameter-level fusion with multi-view teacher weights is presented as a better way to integrate multiple event representations with RGB data.

title: A New Formulation of the Elastica Model with Application to Image Inpainting
summary: Curves and interfaces play a central role in computer vision and image processing, and Euler's elastica energy is one of the most successful tools to model and manipulate them. The elastica energy is usually computed through a level-set or a phase field representation of the curve, in which the curvature term makes the energy nonlinear, non-convex and, in the level-set case, non-differentiable, so that its minimization is notoriously difficult. In this paper, we propose a new formulation of the elastica model based on a binary representation of curves. The key ingredient is a very simple formula for the curvature: if $\phi$ is the $\pm1$ binary function associated with a curve $\Gamma$, then along $\Gamma$ the curvature is given by $-\frac{1}{C_0\epsilon}\left(R_\epsilon *\phi\right)+O(\epsilon)$, where $R_\epsilon$ is a radial kernel supported in a ball of radius $\epsilon$ and $C_0$ is an explicit constant. No derivative of $\phi$ is involved and the convolution is evaluated by FFT. The resulting energy is a weighted total variation, so that formally the new formulation is a generalization of the well-known ROF model; a phase field type model is obtained from the same curvature formula. Combining FFT with the split Bregman iteration, which for the present problem coincides with an augmented Lagrangian method (ALM), we obtain efficient algorithms whose subproblems are either linear systems solved by conjugate gradient or explicit pointwise formulas. Numerical experiments on the inpainting of binary images are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

AI.tldr: The paper reformulates Euler's elastica energy on binary ±1 representations, using a convolution-based curvature formula that yields a weighted total variation model, and solves it with FFT and split Bregman for binary image inpainting.
AI.motivation: Elastica energy is nonlinear, non-convex and, in the level-set case, non-differentiable, which makes its minimization notoriously difficult.
AI.method: For a binary function phi associated with a curve, curvature along the curve is approximated by minus one over (C0 epsilon) times the convolution of a radial kernel R_epsilon with phi plus O(epsilon), with no derivative of phi and convolution evaluated by FFT; the resulting energy generalizes the ROF model, and split Bregman, equivalent to an augmented Lagrangian method here, is combined with conjugate gradient subproblems.
AI.result: The abstract reports that numerical experiments on binary image inpainting demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms, without giving specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: The binary curvature formulation gives efficient algorithms for elastica-based models, with a phase-field variant obtained from the same formula.

title: SpatialVec: A Unified Representation Learning Framework for Geospatial Objects with Boundary-Aware Sampling
comment: Accepted to 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data as a full research paper
summary: Spatial representation learning is essential for Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) applications, enabling machine learning models to capture the geometry, location, and spatial relationships of geographic entities such as points, polylines, and polygons. Existing spatial encoding methods often struggle to preserve fine-grained topological information, particularly for interactions involving complex geometries such as polylines and polygons. These approaches inadequately capture boundary structure and local spatial context, causing topology-sensitive relationships near geometry boundaries to be underrepresented in the learned embedding space. Consequently, accurately modeling complex spatial interactions remains a significant challenge for downstream spatial reasoning tasks. To fill the gap, we introduce SpatialVec, a boundary-aware spatial representation learning framework that adaptively samples geometry boundaries and their surrounding regions, capturing fine-grained geometric structures critical for topology-aware spatial reasoning. A transformer-based encoder-decoder trained through geometry reconstruction produces compact, geometry-aware, and unified representations for points, polylines, and polygons. Empirical evaluation on two real-world datasets shows that SpatialVec substantially improves the preservation of challenging topological relationships involving polygonal interactions and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines significantly on downstream prediction and classification tasks.

AI.tldr: SpatialVec is a boundary-aware transformer encoder-decoder that learns unified representations of points, polylines and polygons by adaptively sampling geometry boundaries and their surroundings, improving topology-sensitive spatial reasoning and downstream prediction.
AI.motivation: Existing spatial encoders fail to preserve fine-grained topology for polylines and polygons, under-representing topology-sensitive relationships near geometry boundaries.
AI.method: The framework adaptively samples geometry boundaries and their surrounding regions and trains a transformer-based encoder-decoder through geometry reconstruction to produce compact, geometry-aware representations for points, polylines and polygons.
AI.result: Evaluated on two real-world datasets, SpatialVec substantially improves preservation of challenging topological relationships involving polygonal interactions and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on downstream prediction and classification tasks.
AI.conclusion: Boundary-aware sampling gives more topology-aware unified representations for GeoAI spatial reasoning.

title: Predicting Cognitive Profiles from Structural MRI using Spatial Graph Representation Learning
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. This work has been submitted to the Elsevier Array for possible publication
summary: Predicting cognitive abilities from structural neuroimaging remains challenging due to the high dimensionality and geometric complexity of brain morphology. Conventional models typically flatten regional morphometry into tabular features, failing to explicitly represent spatial relationships. We propose a Spatial-Topological Graph Neural Network (ST-GNN) to predict four distinct cognitive phenotypes across large pediatric cohorts (N = 2,378 to 2,424). By projecting regional morphometry onto a population-level standardized spatial graph, ST-GNN restricts message passing to defined neighboring regions. Evaluations demonstrate that ST-GNN effectively fuses spatial morphology with systemic covariates, outperforming linear baselines and topology-free deep models. Ablations reveal that imposing a sparse geometric topology (K-nearest neighbors) and utilizing global feature scaling - which preserves absolute morphometric scale - outperform fully connected networks and region-normalized approaches. These choices provide transferable architectural inductive biases, revealing differences between computational routing and morphometric feature attribution. Integrated Gradients analysis identified distinct morphological features consistent with neuroanatomical evidence, such as cerebellar volume for working memory and superior frontal surface area for executive function. These findings suggest standardized structural MRI provides useful information for task-specific cognitive prediction, establishing a foundation for MRI-based neurodevelopmental assessment.

AI.tldr: A Spatial-Topological Graph Neural Network predicts four cognitive phenotypes from structural MRI in large pediatric cohorts by restricting message passing to neighboring regions on a standardized spatial graph, outperforming linear and topology-free baselines.
AI.motivation: Conventional models flatten regional brain morphometry into tabular features and fail to represent spatial relationships explicitly.
AI.method: Regional morphometry is projected onto a population-level standardized spatial graph with K-nearest-neighbor sparse topology and global feature scaling, with message passing limited to defined neighbouring regions; Integrated Gradients is used for attribution.
AI.result: Across cohorts of 2,378 to 2,424 children, ST-GNN outperforms linear baselines and topology-free deep models; sparse KNN topology and global scaling outperform fully connected networks and region-normalized approaches; attributions highlight features such as cerebellar volume for working memory and superior frontal surface area for executive function.
AI.conclusion: Standardized structural MRI carries useful information for task-specific cognitive prediction, providing a basis for MRI-based neurodevelopmental assessment.

title: Brain-Behavior Modeling from Multimodal MRI using Opportunistic Pretraining and Common-Cohort Adaptation
comment: 39 pages, 4 figures. This work has been submitted to the Elsevier NeuroImage for possible publication
summary: Incomplete imaging coverage limits sample sizes for multimodal cognitive prediction. We evaluated a two-stage opportunistic deep ensemble using baseline Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study data to predict fluid, crystallized, and total cognition. Separate neural models processed structural/diffusion, resting-state, and task-based MRI data with covariates. Models were pretrained on eligible modality cohorts (up to 9,686 participants), adapted to common training cohorts, and fused via Ridge regression (trimodal cohort: 4,216 participants). Five-fold family-aware cross-validation compared this approach against constituent and covariate-only models. Two-stage training increased mean test coefficient of determination (R^2) in 24 of 27 comparisons (median gain: 0.0081). Fusion increased mean R^2 by 0.0051-0.0333 over the strongest constituent and reduced mean absolute error by 0.0067-0.0976. Task-plus-resting-state and trimodal ensembles reduced absolute error across all targets (nominal p <= 0.0108). Task-plus-resting-state fusion achieved the highest mean R^2 for fluid (0.2222) and total cognition (0.3665), while structural-plus-resting-state led for crystallized cognition (0.3706), yielding R^2 gains of 0.0805, 0.1180, and 0.0890 over covariate-only references. Ablations showed expanded pretraining drove most improvements. Gradient-based attribution identified target-dependent input patterns. These findings support using partially observed cohorts for model development to achieve modest fusion gains. Pending external validation, this approach may support MRI-informed cognitive phenotyping.

AI.tldr: A two-stage opportunistic deep ensemble fuses structural, resting-state and task MRI models pretrained on partially observed cohorts to predict cognition in ABCD, with modest R^2 gains over covariate-only references.
AI.motivation: Incomplete imaging coverage limits sample sizes for multimodal cognitive prediction, so partially observed cohorts need to be used.
AI.method: Separate neural models process structural/diffusion, resting-state and task MRI with covariates; models are pretrained on eligible modality cohorts (up to 9,686 participants), adapted to common training cohorts, and fused by Ridge regression on a trimodal cohort of 4,216 participants, with five-fold family-aware cross-validation.
AI.result: Two-stage training raises mean test R^2 in 24 of 27 comparisons (median gain 0.0081); fusion increases mean R^2 by 0.0051 to 0.0333 over the strongest constituent; task-plus-resting-state fusion achieves the highest R^2 for fluid (0.2222) and total cognition (0.3665), and structural-plus-resting-state for crystallized cognition (0.3706), giving gains of 0.0805, 0.1180 and 0.0890 over covariate-only references.
AI.conclusion: Partially observed cohorts support model development with modest fusion gains, and expanded pretraining drives most improvements; the approach may support MRI-informed cognitive phenotyping pending external validation.

title: DTP-OPSD: Reinforcement Learning with Distractor-Aware Temporal-Privilege On-Policy Self-Distillation for Temporal Video Grounding
summary: Temporal Video Grounding (TVG) aims to localize the start and end times of an event described by a language query in a video. The task becomes particularly challenging when the same video contains multiple repeated, similar, or opposite events. On these hard examples, all responses sampled by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) may miss the target and receive zero temporal Intersection-over-Union (tIoU). Their group-relative advantages are then all zero, leaving no useful policy gradient signal. To address this, we propose DTP-OPSD, a reinforcement learning framework with distractor-aware temporal-privilege on-policy self-distillation. The student observes the clean video and generates responses on-policy, while a shared-weight teacher observes a privileged video in which the target window is marked by red full-frame borders and same-video distractor windows by blue full-frame borders. For the distillation loss, the teacher evaluates student-generated prefixes and provides dense token-level Jensen-Shannon divergence supervision. This supervision remains informative even when GRPO provides no policy gradient signal. We suppress distillation when the teacher does not outperform the student and strengthen it for groups where the teacher performs better but all student rollouts receive zero tIoU. We also construct a compact hard-interference training set through VLM screening and human verification. With only 300 additional post-training examples, DTP-OPSD achieves the highest mIoU among the compared open-source 8B models on Charades-TimeLens, ActivityNet-TimeLens, and QVHighlights-TimeLens, reaching 55.93, 54.77, and 66.71, respectively. Compared with Pure GRPO trained on the same data, DTP-OPSD improves all 12 reported metrics, with R1@0.7 gains of 1.28, 1.62, and 1.78 points on the three benchmarks. Code will be released at this https URL

AI.tldr: DTP-OPSD is an RL framework for temporal video grounding that adds distractor-aware, privileged-video on-policy self-distillation so that hard examples with zero GRPO gradient still get dense supervision, reaching the highest mIoU among compared open-source 8B models on three TimeLens benchmarks.
AI.motivation: On hard temporal grounding examples with repeated or similar events, all GRPO rollouts can miss the target and receive zero tIoU, leaving no useful policy gradient.
AI.method: A shared-weight teacher observes a privileged video with the target window marked by red borders and same-video distractors by blue borders, and provides token-level Jensen-Shannon divergence supervision on student prefixes; distillation is suppressed when the teacher does not beat the student and strengthened for groups where the teacher is better but all student rollouts get zero tIoU; a compact hard-interference set of 300 examples is built through VLM screening and human verification.
AI.result: DTP-OPSD achieves the highest mIoU among compared open-source 8B models on Charades-TimeLens, ActivityNet-TimeLens and QVHighlights-TimeLens, at 55.93, 54.77 and 66.71; compared with Pure GRPO on the same data it improves all 12 reported metrics, with R1@0.7 gains of 1.28, 1.62 and 1.78 points.
AI.conclusion: Distillation from a privileged teacher supplies useful supervision where GRPO alone gives none, improving temporal grounding in hard, interference-heavy videos; code is to be released.

title: CDBM: Complexity-Diversity Framework for Building Morphology Analysis
summary: We introduce Complexity-Diversity Building Metrics (CDBM), twelve interpretable descriptors for building massings represented as vertical extrusions. They measure how strongly geometric detail is expressed (complexity) and how unevenly it varies across one- and two-dimensional elements (diversity). Computed for 482,241,306 OpenStreetMap buildings and compared with 3D Building Metrics (3DBM) and the LION shape latent on task-specific samples, CDBM is tested on function, region, contextual relevance, real-generated discrimination, human preference and geometry-conditioned generation. With gradient boosting, CDBM best separates generated from mapped massings and best matches human preference; with logistic regression it matches 3DBM on realism. 3DBM leads on the other three tasks. As generation targets, the descriptors show that models struggle to produce strongly expressed and heterogeneous forms. CDBM complements existing indicators.

AI.tldr: CDBM is a set of twelve interpretable descriptors for building massings that measure geometric complexity and diversity, and it best separates generated from mapped massings and matches human preference, while 3DBM leads on the other tasks.
AI.motivation: Building morphology analysis needs interpretable descriptors of how strongly geometric detail is expressed and how unevenly it varies across elements.
AI.method: Twelve Complexity-Diversity Building Metrics are computed for 482,241,306 OpenStreetMap buildings and compared with 3D Building Metrics (3DBM) and the LION shape latent on function, region, contextual relevance, real-generated discrimination, human preference and geometry-conditioned generation tasks, using gradient boosting and logistic regression.
AI.result: With gradient boosting, CDBM best separates generated from mapped massings and best matches human preference; with logistic regression it matches 3DBM on realism; 3DBM leads on the other three tasks; as generation targets, models struggle to produce strongly expressed and heterogeneous forms.
AI.conclusion: CDBM complements existing building indicators.

title: SketchBloom: Training-Free Vector Sketch Outpainting with Stroke-Level Style Control
summary: Outpainting sparse sketches while preserving contour coherence and stroke style remains challenging. We present SketchBloom, a training-free framework that combines pretrained raster outpainting and style-transfer guidance with per-instance vector optimization. Given a sketch, a scene prompt, and an optional reference style, it produces an editable Scalable Vector Graphic (SVG) composed of Bezier strokes. Adaptive latent blending balances content contours and reference texture without model retraining. A reference-derived stroke vocabulary initializes contour- and DINO-attention-guided strokes, which are optimized separately for structure and texture before contour-emphasizing multiply fusion. As in prior optimization-based vector sketching, no task-specific network is trained; our contribution is the synthesis design specialized to sketch outpainting. On LineArtOut-1K, comprising 1,024 input and style combinations, SketchBloom improves perceptual, semantic, and structural fidelity over the evaluated vector baselines when all methods vectorize the same outpainted raster. This protocol evaluates vector synthesis rather than end-to-end outpainting or reference-style superiority. Runtime is approximately six minutes per pair on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: SketchBloom is a training-free framework that outpaints sparse sketches into editable SVG drawings of Bezier strokes, using pretrained raster outpainting, style-transfer guidance and per-instance vector optimization, and improves over evaluated vector baselines on LineArtOut-1K.
AI.motivation: Outpainting sparse sketches while preserving contour coherence and stroke style remains challenging.
AI.method: Given a sketch, a scene prompt and an optional reference style, SketchBloom uses adaptive latent blending between content contours and reference texture, a reference-derived stroke vocabulary initialized with contour- and DINO-attention-guided strokes, separate optimization of structure and texture, and contour-emphasizing multiply fusion, without model retraining.
AI.result: On LineArtOut-1K (1,024 input and style combinations) SketchBloom improves perceptual, semantic and structural fidelity over the evaluated vector baselines when all methods vectorize the same outpainted raster; runtime is about six minutes per pair on one H200 GPU.
AI.conclusion: The contribution is a synthesis design specialized to sketch outpainting that evaluates vector synthesis rather than end-to-end outpainting or reference-style superiority.

title: SketchForge: Training-Free Scene-to-Vector Sketching via Decoupled Structure and Texture Optimization
summary: Converting a raster image into a resolution-independent, stroke-editable vector sketch while faithfully preserving both structural contours and tonal texture remains challenging: raster-space rendering pipelines are difficult to edit at the stroke level, while generation-from-scratch vectorization methods struggle to remain faithful to an arbitrary input image. We present SketchForge, a training-free framework that converts an input raster image into a resolution-independent SVG sketch through per-instance test-time optimization of Bezier curves, requiring no additional training or fine-tuning. Strokes are seeded via a contour and attention-guided initialization, then refined by a vector-native differentiable rendering pipeline that decouples structural contour strokes from free-form texture strokes under dedicated objectives, composited via multiply-blend layering. Extensive experiments show that SketchForge consistently outperforms existing vector-based baselines in structural fidelity and generation quality. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: SketchForge is a training-free framework that converts a raster image into an editable, resolution-independent SVG sketch by optimizing Bezier strokes per image. It reports better structural fidelity and generation quality than existing vector-based baselines.
AI.motivation: Raster-space rendering pipelines are hard to edit at the stroke level, and generation-from-scratch vectorization methods struggle to stay faithful to an arbitrary input image while keeping both contours and tonal texture.
AI.method: Strokes are initialized from contour and attention guidance, then refined with a vector-native differentiable renderer that separates structural contour strokes from free-form texture strokes under dedicated objectives, composited with multiply-blend layering. Per-instance test-time optimization requires no training or fine-tuning.
AI.result: The abstract reports that SketchForge consistently outperforms existing vector-based baselines in structural fidelity and generation quality. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Per-image test-time optimization with decoupled structure and texture strokes offers an editable vector sketch output without any training, making vector sketching faithful to arbitrary inputs.

title: Seeing Less in a Sparse World: Cross-View Geolocalization from Limited Field-of-View Observations
summary: Cross-view geolocalization aims to determine the geographic location of a ground-level image by retrieving its corresponding satellite image, offering a promising alternative for localization in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-denied or degraded environments such as urban canyons, dense forests, and disaster scenarios. Despite recent progress, existing approaches remain limited by the lack of globally diverse training datasets and benchmarks that are often geographically restricted. Furthermore, most benchmarks rely on panoramic ground views, which do not reflect the limited field-of-view imagery captured by real world cameras. To address these challenges, we introduce Cross-View World 500k (CVW500k), a large-scale globally distributed dataset containing over 500,000 ground-satellite image pairs collected across diverse geographic regions and environments. Unlike previous datasets, CVW500k uses limited field-of-view ground images, providing a more realistic and challenging setting for cross-view geolocalization. In addition, we propose GeoQueryNet, a query-based cross-view fusion transformer framework designed to bridge the viewpoint gap between ground and satellite images. The model leverages a CLIP-based visual encoder with parameter-efficient LoRA adaptation and introduces a Cross-View Alignment Module that uses learnable query tokens to extract geographically consistent features across viewpoints. Our code can be found here: this https URL .

AI.tldr: The paper introduces CVW500k, a globally distributed cross-view geolocalization dataset of over 500,000 ground-satellite pairs with limited field-of-view ground images, and GeoQueryNet, a query-based cross-view fusion transformer. Together they target more realistic and harder ground-to-satellite matching.
AI.motivation: Existing cross-view geolocalization datasets are geographically restricted and mostly use panoramic ground views, which do not reflect the limited field-of-view images captured by real cameras.
AI.method: GeoQueryNet uses a CLIP-based visual encoder with parameter-efficient LoRA adaptation and a Cross-View Alignment Module with learnable query tokens that extract geographically consistent features across ground and satellite viewpoints.
AI.result: The abstract does not report quantitative results; it states only that CVW500k provides a more realistic and challenging setting than previous datasets.
AI.conclusion: A large, globally diverse dataset with limited field-of-view ground images, paired with a query-based fusion model, is presented as a more realistic benchmark for cross-view geolocalization in GNSS-denied settings.

title: Seeing the Unseen: Unified Visible--Invisible Motion for Physically Consistent Video Generation
summary: Recent advances in video generation have achieved impressive visual quality, yet they often fail to produce physically consistent dynamics due to the lack of explicit modeling of underlying physical processes. Existing approaches either rely on simulators with strong assumptions or use coarse semantic guidance, and further struggle to effectively inject physical priors into generation models. In this work, we propose Seeing the Unseen, a unified framework for physics-grounded video generation. Our approach decomposes the problem into two stages: learning physical dynamics and injecting them into video synthesis. First, we introduce a lightweight Particle-based Graph Dynamics Simulator (PGDS) that learns generalizable physical interactions from data and predicts plausible 3D motion trajectories. Second, we propose a Visible--Invisible Motion Field (VIMF) that captures both motion observable in the input frame and motion that emerges over time due to object dynamics. This representation enables more complete and structured motion guidance compared to conventional physical signals. By integrating these trajectories into a diffusion-based generator, our method produces videos that are both visually coherent and physically consistent. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved motion accuracy, interaction consistency, and reduced physical artifacts compared to strong baselines.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Seeing the Unseen, a two-stage framework for physics-grounded video generation that learns a lightweight particle-based dynamics simulator and injects its predicted motion into a diffusion video generator. It reports improved motion accuracy, interaction consistency and fewer physical artifacts.
AI.motivation: Video generators reach high visual quality but often produce physically inconsistent dynamics, because they lack explicit physical modeling. Existing approaches rely on simulators with strong assumptions or on coarse semantic guidance.
AI.method: A Particle-based Graph Dynamics Simulator (PGDS) learns physical interactions from data and predicts 3D motion trajectories. A Visible-Invisible Motion Field (VIMF) represents both motion visible in the input frame and motion that emerges over time, and this field guides a diffusion-based generator.
AI.result: The abstract states that experiments show improved motion accuracy, interaction consistency and reduced physical artifacts compared with strong baselines, without giving specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Injecting learned, complete motion fields (visible and invisible) into diffusion generation is presented as a practical route to physically consistent video synthesis.

title: Déjà Vu: Cycle-Consistent Re-ranking for Semantic Correspondence
summary: We propose \emph{Déjà Vu}, a test-time decoding module for semantic correspondence. Matching semantically equivalent keypoints across images of the same object category is challenging due to variations in appearance, viewpoint, and scale. While features from large pretrained vision models carry strong zero-shot correspondence ability, existing methods reduce final matching to greedy top-$1$ nearest-neighbor selection. We show that the correct correspondence appears among the top-ranked candidates far more often than top-$1$ matching achieves: with $30$ candidates, zero-shot features exceed the top-$1$ accuracy of a supervised model. This reveals a \textit{decoding bottleneck} rather than a limit of the representation. Motivated by this observation, we formulate semantic correspondence as a \textit{recall-then-rerank} problem. Our method first nominates an adaptive candidate set, larger when the similarity distribution is ambiguous and smaller when it is confident, then re-ranks the candidates with a graded cycle-consistency score: each candidate is matched back to the source image and penalized by how far its reverse match lands from the original keypoint. The module operates entirely on the similarity matrix already computed by the base method. It consistently improves three representative baselines on SPair-71k, its geometric subset, and PF-Pascal under both unsupervised and weakly supervised settings, with gains of up to $+1.8$ PCK@0.10 on SPair-71k and $+3.4$ PCK@0.15 on PF-Pascal, and $+4.9$ under Keypoint Average Precision.

AI.tldr: Deja Vu is a test-time decoding module for semantic correspondence that replaces greedy top-1 matching with a recall-then-rerank procedure based on graded cycle-consistency. It improves three baselines on SPair-71k, its geometric subset and PF-Pascal.
AI.motivation: Existing methods reduce matching to greedy top-1 nearest-neighbor selection, although the correct correspondence often appears among top-ranked candidates. The authors frame this as a decoding bottleneck rather than a limit of the pretrained representation.
AI.method: The method builds an adaptive candidate set that is larger when the similarity distribution is ambiguous and smaller when it is confident. It re-ranks candidates with a graded cycle-consistency score that penalizes how far each candidate's reverse match lands from the source keypoint. It operates only on the similarity matrix of the base method.
AI.result: It consistently improves three representative baselines on SPair-71k, its geometric subset and PF-Pascal under unsupervised and weakly supervised settings, with gains of up to +1.8 PCK@0.10 on SPair-71k, +3.4 PCK@0.15 on PF-Pascal and +4.9 Keypoint Average Precision. With 30 candidates, zero-shot features exceed the top-1 accuracy of a supervised model.
AI.conclusion: Much of the gap in semantic correspondence lies in the decoding step, and a lightweight, training-free cycle-consistency re-ranker can recover part of it on top of existing methods.

title: SIEVE: Preserving Cross-Image Evidence via Depth-Aware Token Compression
comment: 19 pages, including supplementary material. Code: this https URL
summary: Multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) incur substantial computation when processing long visual sequences. Compressing these sequences must preserve complementary evidence across images and keep tokens from different images separate. Global selection can underrepresent question-relevant images, and pruning in early decoder layers risks removing relevant content before sufficient multimodal processing, yet existing methods spend most of the budget on these early layers. We propose SIEVE, a training-free, single-pass framework that jointly allocates visual tokens across images and decoder depth. SIEVE first pools each image into a compact spatial grid to reduce early processing cost. It then progressively selects representatives using prompt attention under equal per-image quotas and aggregates unselected tokens into similar representatives from the same image. These operations keep every image represented and its tokens separate from other images, while refining the retained representations. A closed-form schedule sets retention counts to target a prescribed average token budget across decoder layers. Across four VLM backbones, SIEVE achieves the highest average at a 6.25% budget on five multi-image benchmarks and four single-image benchmarks, and the highest mean on two video benchmarks. On LLaVA-OneVision-7B, it outperforms the strongest baseline by 9.96 and 9.03 points at 6.25% and 12.5% budgets, and at 12.5% it exceeds the uncompressed model by 2.01 points with 6.6x fewer prefill FLOPs.

AI.tldr: SIEVE is a training-free, single-pass method that compresses visual tokens for multi-image vision-language models by allocating tokens across images and decoder depth. It preserves evidence from every image and reports the highest average at a 6.25% token budget across several benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Multi-image VLMs are costly on long visual sequences. Global selection can underrepresent question-relevant images, and existing methods spend most of the budget on early decoder layers, where pruning may remove relevant content before enough multimodal processing.
AI.method: Each image is pooled into a compact spatial grid. Representatives are selected progressively using prompt attention under equal per-image quotas, and unselected tokens are merged into similar representatives from the same image. A closed-form schedule sets retention counts across decoder layers to meet a target average token budget.
AI.result: Across four VLM backbones, SIEVE achieves the highest average at a 6.25% budget on five multi-image and four single-image benchmarks, and the highest mean on two video benchmarks. On LLaVA-OneVision-7B it beats the strongest baseline by 9.96 and 9.03 points at 6.25% and 12.5% budgets; at 12.5% it exceeds the uncompressed model by 2.01 points with 6.6x fewer prefill FLOPs.
AI.conclusion: Per-image quotas and depth-aware budget scheduling allow large visual token reductions in multi-image VLMs without losing cross-image evidence, and in some settings with no accuracy loss.

title: MoRE-GS: Motion-Regime Experts for Future Gaussian Splatting
summary: Future dynamic novel-view synthesis requires extrapolating multiple motion regimes within the same scene. A single dynamics model may not simultaneously represent stationary regions, coordinated motion, local interactions, and articulated trajectories. We introduce Motion Regime Expert Routing for Gaussian Splatting (MoRE-GS), a causal, render-aware framework for forecasting dynamic 3D Gaussian scenes. MoRE-GS freezes a Gaussian representation reconstructed exclusively from the observed temporal prefix and forecasts its control-keypoint motion using four complementary experts: persistence, a coefficient-space Transformer, a graph convolutional network, and a structured Transformer with rigid and non-rigid motion constraints. A compact routing table assigns expert mixtures across soft motion groups and forecast-horizon bins, while a persistence gate suppresses unreliable extrapolation. Across D-NeRF and HyperNeRF scenes, MoRE-GS achieves improved performance against other methods, and these results demonstrate that renderer-calibrated composition of complementary motion predictors improves causal dynamic Gaussian forecasting across heterogeneous motion regimes. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: MoRE-GS forecasts future dynamic 3D Gaussian scenes by routing among four complementary motion experts with a render-aware, causal framework. It reports improved novel-view synthesis over other methods on D-NeRF and HyperNeRF scenes.
AI.motivation: A single dynamics model may not capture the different motion regimes in one scene, such as stationary regions, coordinated motion, local interactions and articulated trajectories, when extrapolating future dynamic novel views.
AI.method: A Gaussian representation is reconstructed from the observed temporal prefix and frozen. Its control-keypoint motion is forecast by four experts: persistence, a coefficient-space Transformer, a graph convolutional network, and a structured Transformer with rigid and non-rigid constraints. A routing table assigns expert mixtures across soft motion groups and forecast-horizon bins, and a persistence gate suppresses unreliable extrapolation.
AI.result: The abstract reports improved performance against other methods on D-NeRF and HyperNeRF scenes, without giving specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Renderer-calibrated composition of complementary motion predictors is presented as an effective way to improve causal dynamic Gaussian forecasting across heterogeneous motion regimes.

title: Evaluating SAM-based and Convolutional Architectures in Thin Retinal Vessel Segmentation: Model Capacity, Computational Cost and Foundation Pre-training
summary: In retinal vessel segmentation, plain Vision Transformers (ViTs) are commonly expected to perform worse than convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on thin vessels, for reasons such as their coarse patch tokenization, their weak locality bias and their need for large training sets. Although this expectation is widely shared in the literature, how plain ViTs actually compare with CNNs on thin vessels has not been systematically quantified. We address this question by comparing a model with a plain ViT encoder (MedSAM), a hybrid Transformer (LiteMedSAM) and three CNNs of different sizes on three retinal datasets (DRIVE, HRF, FIVES) and, as a second-domain check, a microscopy dataset (VessMap). We measured the centerline recall and precision of thin vessels and compared the models while also considering their computational cost and how many epochs they needed to train. We found that the pre-trained MedSAM had a centerline recall of thin vessels that was not significantly different from that of the best CNN on all four datasets (-0.6 to +2.5 percentage points). A compact plain ViT obtained through architecture search but trained from scratch did not retain this performance. For pre-trained plain ViTs, our results do not support the expectation that they miss thin vessels, although similar thin-vessel performance can be obtained with much smaller models.

AI.tldr: The paper systematically compares a plain ViT (MedSAM), a hybrid Transformer (LiteMedSAM) and three CNNs on thin retinal vessel segmentation. It finds that the pre-trained plain ViT matches the best CNN in centerline recall of thin vessels, contrary to the common expectation.
AI.motivation: It is widely assumed that plain ViTs miss thin vessels because of coarse patch tokenization, weak locality bias and large data needs, but this expectation had not been systematically quantified.
AI.method: Models are compared on DRIVE, HRF and FIVES retinal datasets, with VessMap microscopy as a second-domain check. The evaluation uses centerline recall and precision of thin vessels, together with computational cost and training epochs. A compact plain ViT found by architecture search and trained from scratch is also tested.
AI.result: The pre-trained MedSAM centerline recall on thin vessels is not significantly different from the best CNN on all four datasets (-0.6 to +2.5 percentage points). The architecture-searched ViT trained from scratch does not retain this performance.
AI.conclusion: For pre-trained plain ViTs the results do not support the expectation that they miss thin vessels, and similar thin-vessel performance can be obtained with much smaller models.

title: TAP-Out: Tracking Any Point in 360° via Outpainting
comment: Accepted at BMVC 2026. 22 pages, including supplementary material. Project page: this https URL
summary: Tracking points that leave the camera's field of view (FoV) requires reasoning about unobserved scene dynamics, a fundamentally different problem from tracking visible correspondences. We present TAP-Out, an offline method that makes this out-of-view (OOV) reasoning explicit by leveraging generative video outpainting as a world-model prior. Given a narrow-FoV input video, TAP-Out outpaints a complete 360° equirectangular video, locates target objects within the panoramic scene via video object segmentation, and synthesises object-centred perspective crops on which standard in-frame trackers operate. This decoupled design composes off-the-shelf foundation models without requiring task-specific architectural modifications. On the TAPVid360 benchmark, TAP-Out achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving OOV tracking accuracy by approximately 3x over the best prior method. We demonstrate its flexibility on out-of-frame object segmentation and detection and we provide detailed diagnostic analyses across motion regimes, static versus dynamic content, and hallucination quality, characterising when and why the approach succeeds or fails.

AI.tldr: TAP-Out tracks points that leave the camera's field of view by outpainting the input video into a 360-degree panorama, segmenting the target and tracking on synthesized perspective crops. It reports about 3x better out-of-view tracking accuracy than the best prior method on TAPVid360.
AI.motivation: Tracking points outside the field of view requires reasoning about unobserved dynamics, which is a different problem from tracking visible correspondences, and prior methods handle it poorly.
AI.method: The method is offline and uses generative video outpainting as a world-model prior to produce an equirectangular 360-degree video. Targets are located by video object segmentation in the panorama, and object-centred perspective crops are fed to standard in-frame trackers. It composes off-the-shelf foundation models without task-specific architecture changes.
AI.result: On TAPVid360 it achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving out-of-view tracking accuracy by about 3x over the best prior method. It also transfers to out-of-frame segmentation and detection, and diagnostic analyses cover motion regimes, static versus dynamic content and hallucination quality.
AI.conclusion: Explicit outpainting-based reasoning about unseen regions is an effective and flexible route to out-of-view tracking, and the paper characterizes when it succeeds or fails.

title: PAM-Mamba - Efficient Dense Action Detection using Mamba
summary: Dense action detection requires precisely localising multiple overlapping actions in long untrimmed videos. Transformer-based methods achieve strong accuracy but their $O(T^2)$ self-attention cost limits scalability. We present PAM-Mamba, a linear-time $O(T)$ architecture built on Mamba with a multi-branch temporal encoder. Gated Learnable Positional Encoding (GLPE) controls positional signal injection via a scalar gate initialised to zero, starting training without added positional signal. A Hub-and-Spoke Funnel extends the non-hierarchical multi-scale design of PAT with a direct residual from the original full-resolution input to each coarse branch, providing each coarse branch with a projection of the input features. Bi-TemBa (Bidirectional Temporal Mamba) first extracts local motion cues with a shallow Temporal Convolution Module, then applies a cascaded bidirectional Mamba scan; the backward pass refines the forward-scanned representation from the opposite direction, giving each temporal position access to context from both directions in linear time. Uncertainty-Based Mixup uses prediction entropy to guide the selection of mixup partners. Using the PAT evaluation implementation, we obtain 26.82 (Charades I3D), 34.59 (Charades CLIP), 46.56 (MultiTHUMOS I3D), and 46.92 mAP (MultiTHUMOS CLIP), with 26.1-27.9M parameters, 61-63% fewer than PAT.

AI.tldr: PAM-Mamba is a linear-time, O(T), dense action detector built on Mamba with a multi-branch temporal encoder. It reports mAP of 26.82 and 34.59 on Charades (I3D and CLIP) and 46.56 and 46.92 on MultiTHUMOS, with 61-63% fewer parameters than PAT.
AI.motivation: Transformer-based dense action detection is accurate but its O(T^2) self-attention cost limits scalability to long untrimmed videos.
AI.method: Components include Gated Learnable Positional Encoding with a scalar gate initialized to zero, a Hub-and-Spoke Funnel that adds a direct residual from the full-resolution input to each coarse branch, and Bi-TemBa, which combines a shallow temporal convolution module with a cascaded bidirectional Mamba scan. Uncertainty-Based Mixup selects mixup partners using prediction entropy.
AI.result: Using the PAT evaluation implementation, mAP is 26.82 (Charades I3D), 34.59 (Charades CLIP), 46.56 (MultiTHUMOS I3D) and 46.92 (MultiTHUMOS CLIP), with 26.1-27.9M parameters, 61-63% fewer than PAT.
AI.conclusion: A linear-time Mamba-based temporal encoder with these design choices is presented as a more efficient alternative to Transformers for dense action detection, with fewer parameters.

title: Spoofing the Latent State: Imperceptible Goal-Image Attacks Derail Planning in LeWorldModel
summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) have recently emerged as general-purpose visual world models for control. A prominent example is LeWorldModel (LeWM), which trains end-to-end from pixels using an isotropic Gaussian anti-collapse regularizer (SIGReg) and plans by minimizing the squared Euclidean distance between predicted and goal embeddings. In this work, we investigate the test-time robustness of this latent planning interface. Analyzing the learned metric on Push-T, we first find that task-relevant object state heavily dominates latent distance: shifting the block by a single pixel displaces the embedding $3\times$ further than an equivalent agent shift, and swapping the block pose alone accounts for $99\%$ of the distance between scene pairs. However, because this pose information is distributed across a curved, high-dimensional manifold rather than a fixed linear subspace, the encoder cannot be trivially edited post-hoc to isolate or redirect it. We next demonstrate that this geometry is highly vulnerable at test time. A white-box $\ell_\infty$ perturbation of just $\epsilon{=}4/255$ applied to a single input frame causes the encoder to register the block at an arbitrary, attacker-chosen pose in $73$--$95\%$ of scenes without disturbing the encoded agent state. Perturbing either the goal image or the live camera observation drops Push-T planning success from $87\%$ to $32\%$, whereas uniform random noise at twice the magnitude has negligible impact. This vulnerability persists across all four standard LeWM benchmarks (Push-T, Two-Room, Reacher, and OGBench-Cube). At $\epsilon{=}8/255$, the attack bridges $82$--$97\%$ of the squared latent distance to the target embedding in every environment, inducing planning degradation proportional to each task's reliance on the spoofed entity.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the latent planning interface of the LeWorldModel JEPA world model is highly vulnerable at test time: a small imperceptible perturbation of one input frame can move the encoded block to an attacker-chosen pose and sharply degrade planning success. The attack is effective across four standard LeWM benchmarks.
AI.motivation: LeWorldModel plans by minimizing squared Euclidean distance between predicted and goal embeddings, and the robustness of this latent planning interface at test time had not been studied.
AI.method: The authors analyze the learned metric on Push-T, showing that object pose dominates latent distance. They then apply a white-box l-infinity perturbation of 4/255 (and 8/255) to a single input frame and measure whether the encoder registers the block at a chosen pose and how much planning degrades.
AI.result: At epsilon 4/255 the encoder places the block at an attacker-chosen pose in 73-95% of scenes without disturbing agent state. Perturbing the goal image or live observation drops Push-T planning success from 87% to 32%, while uniform random noise of twice the magnitude has negligible impact. At 8/255 the attack bridges 82-97% of the squared latent distance to the target, across all four benchmarks (Push-T, Two-Room, Reacher, OGBench-Cube).
AI.conclusion: Latent planning with JEPA world models is fragile to adversarially structured, imperceptible perturbations, so robustness of the embedding geometry needs explicit evaluation before deployment in control.

title: Real-VAS: a Real-World Video Amodal Segmentation Dataset
comment: 34 pages, including supplementary material. Project page: this https URL
summary: Amodal video object segmentation is fundamentally limited by the absence of datasets that combine real-world complexity with precise ground-truth annotations. To address this, we present Real Video Amodal Segmentation (Real-VAS), a new large-scale, zero-shot evaluation dataset built from composited real-image video. We introduce a novel data generation pipeline that enables the creation of programmatically consistent amodal ground truth for real-world footage, in which the object mask, occlusion boundary, and composited image are all derived from a single unoccluded source, without relying on human estimation or expensive 3D reconstruction. Our dataset is structured into two challenging scenarios: dynamic Occlusion, created by compositing two clips of moving objects, and a unique Container category featuring complex, physically constrained interactions.
