These container scenarios--On Surface Containment, Articulated Containment, and Mobile Containment--allow us to generate precise ground truth by simulating an object's motion based on its container's tracked transformation. As a result, Real-VAS provides a diverse and challenging benchmark for evaluating amodal segmentation models on realistic video with the precision of synthetic data. The dataset and our generation code will be made publicly available.

AI.tldr: Real-VAS is a zero-shot evaluation dataset for video amodal segmentation, built by compositing real-image video so that exact amodal ground truth is available without human estimation or 3D reconstruction. It has dynamic occlusion and container scenarios.
AI.motivation: Amodal video segmentation lacks datasets that combine real-world complexity with precise ground-truth annotations, because manual annotation is imprecise and 3D reconstruction is costly.
AI.method: A data generation pipeline derives the object mask, occlusion boundary and composited image from a single unoccluded source. The dataset has two scenarios: dynamic occlusion from two composited moving-object clips, and a Container category with on-surface, articulated and mobile containment, where ground truth comes from the container's tracked transformation.
AI.result: The abstract reports no quantitative results, only the dataset construction and its challenge categories.
AI.conclusion: Real-VAS offers a diverse benchmark with synthetic-level annotation precision on realistic video. The dataset and generation code are stated to be released publicly.

title: PRISM-Net: Dynamic Routing Network with VLM-Guided Disentangled Attribute Distillation for Explainable Fine-Grained Product Retrieval
summary: Fine-grained visual product retrieval in large-scale e-commerce multimedia systems demands discriminative representations capable of simultaneously resolving macro-level category semantics and micro-level visual attributes such as structural contour (line) and chromatic appearance (color). However, conventional backbones including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision Transformers (ViTs) inherently suffer from feature entanglement and shortcut learning. To learn the micro-level visual attributes without costly manual attribute annotations, we propose phase-routed interpretable semantic mixture-of-experts network (PRISM-Net), an explainable multi-expert architecture that disentangles holistic visual features into disentangled line and color expert pathways governed by a conditional meta-router. In phase 1, we introduce an external VLM-Guided sigmoid semantic distillation mechanism with gradient-detached routing gates, utilizing zero-shot text prompts from SigLIP to supervise specialized structural and chromatic experts. In phase 2, the disentangled expert embeddings are adaptively fused with macro base features via a learned meta-router gate to calibrate category boundaries. Extensive 5-fold cross-validation across 275,454 e-commerce images (18 categories) and full-scale retrieval benchmarks (55,091 queries against a 220,363-image gallery) across SwinV2, ConvNeXt-V2, and DINOv3 demonstrate substantial gains. On SwinV2, PRISM-Net boosts full-fold product mAP@10 from 80.98% to 83.90% (+2.92%), line mAP@10 by +5.74%, and color mAP@10 by +9.12%. Furthermore, unsupervised distribution analysis of the meta-router gate reveals that both ViT and CNN backbones emergently allocate up to 6.8x higher structural line weights to rigid appliances and hardware while dedicating >96% chromatic weight to clothing.

AI.tldr: PRISM-Net is an explainable mixture-of-experts network for fine-grained e-commerce product retrieval that separates structural line and chromatic color experts under a meta-router. On SwinV2 it raises full-fold product mAP@10 from 80.98% to 83.90%.
AI.motivation: CNN and ViT backbones suffer from feature entanglement and shortcut learning, which hurts fine-grained retrieval that depends on micro-level attributes such as line and color, and attribute annotations are costly.
AI.method: Phase 1 uses VLM-guided sigmoid semantic distillation with gradient-detached routing gates, using zero-shot SigLIP text prompts to supervise structural and chromatic experts. Phase 2 fuses the disentangled expert embeddings with macro base features through a learned meta-router gate.
AI.result: On SwinV2, product mAP@10 rises from 80.98% to 83.90% (+2.92%), with line mAP@10 up 5.74% and color mAP@10 up 9.12%. Experiments use 5-fold cross-validation on 275,454 images across 18 categories, and retrieval over 55,091 queries against a 220,363-image gallery, across SwinV2, ConvNeXt-V2 and DINOv3. Router analysis shows up to 6.8x higher line weight for rigid appliances and over 96% color weight for clothing.
AI.conclusion: Disentangled expert pathways with a learned meta-router improve fine-grained product retrieval across backbones, and the router's emergent allocation gives an interpretable view of which attributes each category relies on.

title: Spatial Uncertainty Analytics for Budget-Limited Inspection of Hyperspectral Scenes
summary: Land-cover maps classified from wide-area hyperspectral surveys are least reliable along class boundaries and in ambiguous regions, so their errors are spatially structured. We study how this structure can direct a limited verification budget: when a low-altitude UAV or a ground crew can visit only a handful of sites, where it should go depends on how classifier uncertainty is arranged across the scene and how a fixed sensor footprint tiles that arrangement. We estimate a per-pixel uncertainty surface from the disagreement of an ensemble of spectral classifiers and select sites by greedy, field-of-view-aware coverage of the uncertainty mass. On seven benchmark scenes, the highest-uncertainty decile of pixels is 2.6 to 7.9 times richer in errors than the scene as a whole, and the coverage greedy covers up to 57% of the classifier's errors with 15 sites, 1.7 to 18 times as many as uncertainty-agnostic sampling of the same labelled region. A non-overlapping selection of the footprints richest in uncertainty does equally well, so the gain comes from scoring whole footprints by uncertainty mass. The advantage persists under spatially blocked evaluation and with a spectral-spatial classifier, although disagreement then ranks errors less well. It requires restricting the surface to labelled land cover: over the whole scene, disagreement peaks on unlabelled ground, where inspections cannot be scored. The best policy for covering connected high-uncertainty regions depends on the scene and on the threshold that defines them, and Gaussian-process selection covers less uncertainty than the coverage greedy on every scene. The pipeline runs on commodity CPUs.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that disagreement among a spectral classifier ensemble can guide a limited inspection budget by scoring field-of-view footprints by uncertainty mass. With 15 sites the coverage greedy covers up to 57% of classifier errors.
AI.motivation: Land-cover maps from hyperspectral surveys are least reliable at class boundaries and in ambiguous regions, and a UAV or ground crew can visit only a few sites, so where to inspect needs to be decided.
AI.method: A per-pixel uncertainty surface is estimated from disagreement among an ensemble of spectral classifiers. Sites are chosen by greedy, field-of-view-aware coverage of this uncertainty mass, and the surface is restricted to labelled land cover. Gaussian-process selection and other policies are compared.
AI.result: On seven benchmark scenes, the top uncertainty decile is 2.6 to 7.9 times richer in errors than the scene average. With 15 sites the coverage greedy covers up to 57% of errors, 1.7 to 18 times as many as uncertainty-agnostic sampling. Gaussian-process selection covers less uncertainty than the coverage greedy on every scene.
AI.conclusion: Scoring whole footprints by uncertainty mass drives the gain, and the approach runs on commodity CPUs. Its benefit persists under spatially blocked evaluation, though the best policy depends on the scene.

title: A Straight Line Is Not a Camera Pose: Auditing Short-Clip Pose Benchmarks
comment: 34 pages (8-page main text and appendix), 7 figures, 21 tables
summary: The absolute trajectory error (ATE) is the standard measure of camera-motion accuracy, from SLAM to feed-forward 3D reconstruction. On the common Sintel protocol, a constant-velocity straight line using no images has a lower mean ATE than 10 of 11 recent models re-run with official code. Two properties of ATE's alignment explain this. First, it maps any constant-velocity prediction onto the best-fitting line through the true path, so the line scores the path's regression residual. A residual signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) criterion predicts when moving a prediction towards its constant-velocity fit lowers ATE. It gives the outcome for 95% of 1056 model-clip pairs, 98% of 792 held-out pairs and 97% of 1034 ScanNet pairs, and it separates Sintel (median SNR 0.86) from TUM, ScanNet and full-length Bonn and Wild-SLAM (2.7 to 27), where straightening raises every model's mean ATE. Second, position-only alignment ignores where cameras look: rotating a trajectory by 30 degrees against its orientations leaves ATE unchanged, yet worsens the reprojection of static points for every model on Sintel, TUM and ScanNet in the main setting, and the line, second by mean ATE on Sintel, places them worst by geometric mean: a lower ATE need not mean better geometry. Fitting the alignment's rotation to the predicted orientations gives pose-anchored ATE, a one-function change in ATE's units costing 0.17 ms per clip (ATE: 0.11 ms). It ranks every image-free reference below every model on Sintel, tracks the reprojection error under rotation and straightening, where ATE does not (Spearman 0.61 vs. 0.32), largely preserves the models' order, and ties 10-frame translational relative pose error (RPE) and the discernible trajectory error (DTE) on our rotation and reference tests. Code, predictions and results will be released.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that a constant-velocity straight line, using no images, beats most recent models on mean ATE on the Sintel protocol, and it proposes pose-anchored ATE, a rotation-aware variant that better tracks geometric error.
AI.motivation: ATE is the standard camera-motion accuracy measure, but its position-only alignment ignores camera orientation, and it can reward trajectories that are geometrically poor.
AI.method: The authors give a residual signal-to-noise criterion that predicts when straightening a prediction lowers ATE, validated on 1056 model-clip pairs, 792 held-out pairs and 1034 ScanNet pairs. Pose-anchored ATE fits the alignment rotation to the predicted orientations, changing one function at 0.17 ms per clip.
AI.result: On Sintel a straight line has lower mean ATE than 10 of 11 recent models re-run with official code. Sintel has median SNR 0.86, versus 2.7 to 27 on TUM, ScanNet and full-length Bonn and Wild-SLAM. Pose-anchored ATE ranks every image-free reference below every model on Sintel and tracks reprojection error better than ATE (Spearman 0.61 vs. 0.32).
AI.conclusion: Short-clip camera pose benchmarks can be dominated by trajectory shape, so ATE alone is not a reliable measure of geometry. Pose-anchored ATE is proposed as a cheap correction that ties more closely with reprojection error.

title: Selecting or Solving? What Best-of-N Verification Delivers in Video Reasoning
summary: Answering a complex question about a long video is a grounding problem: the answer turns on a few seconds of evidence, and vision-language models remain well below human accuracy at finding them. The standard way to spend extra test-time compute on this kind of video reasoning is best-of-N selection: sample several chain-of-thought answers from a fixed model, then let a second model re-watch the video and pick one. Such pipelines are reported by a single headline number, their margin over a majority vote. That number conflates two effects with opposite deployment consequences: the benefit the second model adds by selecting among candidates, and the benefit it would have supplied by solving the question itself. We separate them, measuring the Selection Increment (SI) -- selection accuracy minus the same verifier's accuracy with the candidates withheld -- alongside the margin over self-consistency, across five long-video benchmarks. The Selection Increment is largest for the weakest verifiers: a verifier that solves poorly on its own leaves the candidates the most room to help. Beating the majority vote follows the opposite profile: where the vote already sits near its ceiling no verifier we test improves on it; below that ceiling only the strongest do. On Video-Holmes, the two come apart on a single pool of candidates -- a weak verifier gains +19.3 points from the candidates yet lands 7.1 points below the vote, while the frontier verifier gains the least and beats the vote. The weakest verifier also shows a failure mode: on EgoSchema it picks by where an option sits in the list rather than by what the video shows. Read as a merit score, SI puts a verifier that fails to beat a majority vote at the top of its ranking; read as an audit, it says which of the two effects a headline number delivers. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper separates two effects of best-of-N verification in long-video reasoning: the Selection Increment (SI) and the benefit of solving the question directly. It shows that weak verifiers gain the most from candidates but can still fall below a majority vote.
AI.motivation: Headline gains of best-of-N pipelines over majority vote conflate the verifier's selection benefit with its own solving ability, and these two effects have different deployment implications.
AI.method: SI is defined as selection accuracy minus the same verifier's accuracy with candidates withheld, reported alongside the margin over self-consistency, across five long-video benchmarks.
AI.result: SI is largest for the weakest verifiers. On Video-Holmes a weak verifier gains +19.3 points from candidates yet lands 7.1 points below the majority vote, while the frontier verifier gains least and beats the vote. On EgoSchema the weakest verifier picks answers by option position rather than video content. Where the vote is near its ceiling, no tested verifier improves on it.
AI.conclusion: SI is a useful audit of which effect a headline number reflects, and as a merit score it ranks verifiers that fail to beat majority vote at the top, so it should be read with that in mind.

title: SASFormer: Stage-Aware Selective Attention Transformer for All-in-One Blind Image Restoration
comment: Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
summary: All-in-one image restoration aims to recover high-quality images from multiple degradation types using a single unified model. Recent methods improve unified restoration with hybrid attention, prompt learning, or routing mechanisms, but generally focus on enhancing degradation adaptivity while employing similar feature modeling strategies across network stages. Consequently, the distinct representation requirements of encoding and decoding under diverse degradations remain insufficiently explored. In this paper, we propose SASFormer, a Stage-Aware Selective Attention Transformer for all-in-one blind image restoration. SASFormer follows a stage-aware design principle: the encoder uses established hybrid channel-spatial attention to build robust content-preserving and degradation-aware representations, while the decoder employs adaptive selective attention for restoration-oriented reconstruction. To address the stage-specific requirements of decoder reconstruction, we develop Adaptive Selective Channel Self-Attention (ASCSA) and Adaptive Selective Spatial Self-Attention (ASSSA), enabling the decoder to dynamically identify restoration-relevant channel responses and spatial contexts. Specifically, ASCSA performs adaptive query-channel selection and attention masking, while ASSSA adaptively integrates spatial attention across multiple window sizes. Compact implicit prompts further modulate the selection process without requiring explicit degradation labels. Extensive experiments on 3-, 5-, and 11-degradation settings demonstrate that SASFormer achieves strong restoration performance with favorable parameter efficiency. Moreover, stage-wise representation analysis and ablation studies provide empirical support for the proposed stage-aware design and the effectiveness of decoder-side adaptive selection.

AI.tldr: SASFormer is an all-in-one blind image restoration Transformer that uses hybrid attention in the encoder and adaptive selective attention in the decoder. It targets the different representation needs of encoding and decoding under multiple degradation types.
AI.motivation: Existing unified restoration methods improve degradation adaptivity but use similar feature modeling across all network stages, leaving the distinct needs of encoding and decoding under diverse degradations unexplored.
AI.method: The encoder uses hybrid channel-spatial attention. The decoder uses Adaptive Selective Channel Self-Attention (ASCSA), which performs query-channel selection and attention masking, and Adaptive Selective Spatial Self-Attention (ASSSA), which integrates spatial attention across multiple window sizes. Compact implicit prompts modulate selection without explicit degradation labels.
AI.result: The abstract reports strong restoration performance with favorable parameter efficiency in 3-, 5- and 11-degradation settings, supported by stage-wise representation analysis and ablations. It gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: A stage-aware design, with selective attention in the decoder, is presented as an effective principle for all-in-one restoration.

title: 3D Neural Rendering for Automated Ultrasonic Laser Scans
summary: Laser doppler vibrometer (LDV) scans can be used to detect defects and cracks in manufactured parts before they are deployed. This work presents a method for reconstructing the steady-state surface wavefield of a three-dimensional part by combining automated robotic manipulation with neural rendering. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic manipulator (UFactory xArm6) with an embedded piezoelectric transducer presented an acoustically excited test article to a stationary LDV at a sequence of known orientations, yielding a set of complex-valued 2D scans with poses derived analytically from the arm kinematics rather than from image-based pose estimation. These scans were used to train a novel complex-nerfacto model, a modified Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) pipeline that replaces the standard three-channel RGB output head with a two-channel output. Complex-nerfacto represents the real and imaginary velocity components of a wavefield, preserving the complex measurement without quantization. Reconstructions of a welded aluminum cylinder and a welded T-bracket were evaluated against measured scans using Z-normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC). The complex-valued pipeline achieved a mean ZNCC of 0.60 at held-out viewing angles, compared with 0.28 for a baseline RGB nerfacto model trained on rendered images of the same data. The resulting surface wavefield reconstructions supported defect detection and characterization on complex components. We identify geometry reconstruction from sparse LDV scans as the remaining obstacle to practical deployment.

AI.tldr: The paper reconstructs steady-state surface wavefields of 3D parts from laser Doppler vibrometer scans by training a complex-valued NeRF variant on poses from robot kinematics. The reconstructed wavefields reach a mean ZNCC of 0.60 at held-out angles, versus 0.28 for an RGB baseline.
AI.motivation: LDV scans can reveal defects and cracks in manufactured parts, but reconstructing a full 3D surface wavefield from scans taken at many orientations is needed for inspection of complex components.
AI.method: A 6-DOF xArm6 robot with an embedded piezoelectric transducer presents an excited test article to a stationary LDV at known orientations. Poses come from arm kinematics, not image-based estimation. Complex-nerfacto replaces the RGB output head with a two-channel head representing the real and imaginary velocity components.
AI.result: The complex-valued pipeline achieves a mean ZNCC of 0.60 at held-out viewing angles on a welded aluminum cylinder and a welded T-bracket, compared with 0.28 for a baseline RGB nerfacto trained on rendered images of the same data.
AI.conclusion: The reconstructions support defect detection and characterization, and the authors identify geometry reconstruction from sparse LDV scans as the remaining obstacle to practical deployment.

title: RATR: Training-Free Material Rebinding via Role Assignment and Temporal Routing
summary: Material rebinding aims to transfer the material appearance from a reference image while preserving the target object's geometry and identity. Existing methods typically struggle to balance material fidelity with structural preservation due to the coupled influence of structural and appearance cues in their visual conditions. We identify role entanglement in the target and reference conditions as a contributing factor the target condition carries both geometry and its original appearance while the reference condition contains material cues alongside object-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose RATR, a training-free material rebinding method built on a diffusion-based image editor that assigns complementary roles to the two conditions and coordinates their influence during denoising. To make the target condition primarily convey structure, we introduce an albedo-resolved surface release mechanism, which suppresses the target's original surface appearance while retaining geometric cues, yielding a structure-oriented condition for material transfer. On the reference side, the designed material evidence isolation mechanism emphasizes material cues while reducing interference from object-specific structure, yielding a complementary material-oriented condition.

AI.tldr: RATR is a training-free material rebinding method that transfers the material appearance of a reference image onto a target object while preserving its geometry, using a diffusion-based image editor with complementary roles for the two conditions.
AI.motivation: Material rebinding methods struggle to balance material fidelity with structural preservation because the target and reference conditions entangle structure and appearance cues, which the authors identify as the cause.
AI.method: An albedo-resolved surface release mechanism suppresses the target's original surface appearance while keeping geometric cues, giving a structure-oriented condition. A material evidence isolation mechanism emphasizes material cues on the reference side while reducing object-specific structure, giving a material-oriented condition. The two conditions are coordinated during denoising.
AI.result: The abstract ends before describing quantitative results, so no numbers are reported here.
AI.conclusion: Assigning complementary roles to target and reference conditions is presented as a way to separate structure from material in training-free material rebinding.

title: Spatial-Spectral Interactive POCS Network for Large-Gap Seismic Data Interpolation
summary: Large gaps in seismic acquisition disrupt reflection events and hinder spectral recovery. Existing seismic interpolation deep unfolding networks primarily rely on localized spatial priors, limiting their ability to aggregate the global context necessary for reconstructing these extensive missing regions. We propose a spatial-spectral interactive projection-onto-convex-sets network (SSI-POCS) to tackle this severely ill-posed problem. By unfolding the classical iterative solver, our network integrates physical consistency with dual-domain deep priors via learned transforms, soft thresholding, and exact data reinsertion. Within the learned prior, a spatial Restormer branch captures local waveform structures, while a fast Fourier convolution (FFC) branch extracts global context, effectively suppressing incoherent components and enhancing spectral energy concentration in the $f-k$ domain. A dual-domain fusion module exchanges these complementary features via bidirectional channel attention and gated modulation, yielding substantial interpolation improvements. To overcome the severe loss of lateral continuity caused by large gaps, we introduce structural similarity (SSIM) supervision, complemented by focal frequency loss (FFL) and transform consistency constraints to suppress incoherent high-frequency components and regularize training. Experiments on a synthetic salt dome and a North Sea field dataset under 50% random and consecutive trace removal demonstrate the effectiveness of SSI-POCS. It significantly enhances event continuity across large gaps and mitigates artifacts, achieving a 3.285~dB SNR improvement over the best competing method while reducing parameters by 75.66%.

AI.tldr: SSI-POCS is a deep-unfolding network for large-gap seismic data interpolation that combines physical data consistency with a dual-domain spatial and Fourier prior. It reports a 3.285 dB SNR improvement over the best competing method with 75.66% fewer parameters.
AI.motivation: Existing seismic interpolation unfolding networks rely on local spatial priors, which cannot aggregate the global context needed to fill large missing regions.
AI.method: The classical POCS solver is unfolded with learned transforms, soft thresholding and exact data reinsertion. The learned prior has a spatial Restormer branch for local waveform structure and a fast Fourier convolution branch for global context. A dual-domain fusion module exchanges features through bidirectional channel attention and gated modulation. Training uses SSIM supervision with focal frequency loss and transform consistency constraints.
AI.result: On a synthetic salt dome and a North Sea field dataset with 50% random and consecutive trace removal, SSI-POCS improves event continuity and reduces artifacts, with a 3.285 dB SNR improvement over the best competing method and 75.66% fewer parameters.
AI.conclusion: Combining global Fourier context with local spatial priors inside an unfolded physics-consistent solver is presented as an effective approach to large-gap seismic interpolation.

title: Structured Channel Network Pruning with Bi-Sparse Matrix Factorization
summary: Structured channel pruning for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) plays an important role in pattern recognition and deep learning. Nevertheless, existing methods usually calculate channel importance scores based on the magnitudes of individual filters, making it difficult to distinguish shared redundancy from individual channel contributions. To tackle this limitation, we propose a novel structured channel pruning method termed bi-sparse matrix factorization (BSMF). Specifically, BSMF characterizes the convolutional weight matrix as output-channel coefficients over a shared basis with row-wise $\ell_{2,p}$-norm and column-wise $\ell_{2,q}$-norm regularization terms, respectively. Note that $p,q\in[0,1)$, which, to our best knowledge, has not been explored in the literature. To solve the resulting non-convex optimization problem, we develop an efficient update scheme built upon the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), in which all subproblems admit closed-form solutions. After that, a compact CNN is obtained by reconstructing the convolutional filters from the learned factors and discarding the redundant channels. Extensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K datasets demonstrate that our proposed BSMF achieves significant network compression while maintaining high reconstruction accuracy. The source code is publicly available at this https URL

AI.tldr: BSMF is a structured channel pruning method for CNNs that factorizes each convolutional weight matrix into shared-basis coefficients under row and column sparsity norms, solved with ADMM. It targets redundancy shared across channels, which per-filter magnitude scores miss.
AI.motivation: Existing channel pruning scores channels by individual filter magnitude, which makes it hard to separate shared redundancy from each channel's own contribution.
AI.method: The weight matrix is characterized as output-channel coefficients over a shared basis, with row-wise l2,p and column-wise l2,q norm regularization where p and q lie in [0,1). An ADMM scheme with closed-form subproblem solutions handles the non-convex problem. A compact CNN is rebuilt from the learned factors, and redundant channels are discarded.
AI.result: The abstract reports significant network compression with high reconstruction accuracy on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K, without specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Bi-sparse factorization with exponents below one is presented as a practical way to compress CNNs by pruning channels on a shared basis, with code publicly available.

title: Words Before Pixels: Selective Modality Routing for Vision-Language Model Unlearning
summary: Vision-language model (VLM) unlearning is often treated as an objective-design problem: given multimodal forget data, the goal is to optimize a loss that removes undesirable behavior while preserving retained capabilities. We argue that this view overlooks an equally important data-centric question: how should each forget example be represented before optimization? Existing methods typically keep image-conditioned failures in their original image-text form, implicitly assuming that pixels are the right route for unlearning whenever pixels appear in the input. We challenge this assumption by constructing modality-decomposed versions of VLM benchmarks, enabling controlled comparisons among image-only, text-only, and multimodal representations of the same examples. Our modality-mixing experiments show that unsafe instruction-following behavior is more effectively suppressed through textual representations than through images alone, while purely text-only unlearning can still weaken visual grounding when the target behavior depends on visual evidence. Motivated by this trade-off, we introduce ModRoute, a gradient-guided per-sample modality routing strategy that selectively converts high visual-pressure examples to text-only form while keeping the remaining examples multimodal. Notably, on VLGuard with LLaVA-1.5-7B, ModRoute has the strongest composite unlearning-utility score of 0.847 at $\gamma=0.5$, a 2.5% improvement over the best random-switching score and $\geq$46% better than pure multimodal or text unlearning. Overall, our results show that effective VLM unlearning depends not only on the objective, but also on the composition and per-sample modality routing of the unlearning data.

AI.tldr: ModRoute is a gradient-guided, per-sample modality routing strategy for VLM unlearning that converts high visual-pressure forget examples to text-only form. It reports the strongest composite unlearning-utility score on VLGuard with LLaVA-1.5-7B.
AI.motivation: VLM unlearning is usually treated as an objective-design problem, while how each forget example is represented, as image-text or text-only, is overlooked. Image-conditioned failures are typically kept in their multimodal form.
AI.method: Modality-decomposed versions of VLM benchmarks allow controlled comparison of image-only, text-only and multimodal representations of the same examples. Based on these results, ModRoute uses gradient guidance to select per-sample which high visual-pressure examples to convert to text-only, keeping the others multimodal.
AI.result: On VLGuard with LLaVA-1.5-7B, ModRoute has the strongest composite unlearning-utility score of 0.847 at gamma=0.5, a 2.5% improvement over the best random-switching score and at least 46% better than pure multimodal or text unlearning.
AI.conclusion: Effective VLM unlearning depends on the composition and per-sample modality routing of the forget data, as well as on the objective.

title: Regularized Wasserstein Distance for Discrete Generative Modeling and Clustering Analysis
summary: In this paper, we formulate clustering analysis as discrete generative modeling. Specifically, when the generator is restricted to a finite candidate space, the generated samples naturally emerge as the most representative prototypes of the underlying data distribution. To model such a discrete candidate space, we employ a Discrete Distribution Network (DDN). However, DDN suffers from unstable training due to its hard nearest-neighbor selection. To stabilize training and encourage geometric consistency, we replace DDN's l2 loss between images with regularized Wasserstein distance between the empirical distributions of real and generated images. The resulting framework, termed Discrete Generative Clustering (DGC), offers four notable advantages: 1) the learned cluster centers are directly interpretable, as they are realistic synthetic samples; 2) the inference cost scales logarithmically with the number of clusters, i.e., O(log K), making the method scalable to extremely large K; 3) the regularized Wasserstein distance provides a smooth and well-behaved optimization objective that facilitates stable convergence, whereas DDN's l2 loss tends to converge to poor local optima; and 4) DGC replaces DDN's nearest-neighbor selection with random-neighbor selection, which avoids the density shift problem during multi-step forward. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and desirable properties of DGC. The code is publicly available at GitHub.

AI.tldr: The paper frames clustering as discrete generative modeling and proposes Discrete Generative Clustering (DGC), which replaces the l2 loss in a Discrete Distribution Network with a regularized Wasserstein distance. Cluster centers are realistic samples and inference scales as O(log K).
AI.motivation: Discrete Distribution Networks are unstable to train because of hard nearest-neighbor selection, and their l2 image loss tends to converge to poor local optima.
AI.method: The l2 loss is replaced by a regularized Wasserstein distance between the empirical distributions of real and generated images, and nearest-neighbor selection is replaced by random-neighbor selection to avoid density shift during multi-step forward generation.
AI.result: The abstract states that extensive experiments on several benchmarks show the effectiveness and desirable properties of DGC, without giving specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Clustering as discrete generation yields interpretable, realistic prototypes and scalable inference (O(log K)) to very large numbers of clusters, and the code is publicly available.

title: SE-Mem: Semantic-Episodic Memory for Scene-Consistent Generative View Synthesis
summary: Generative view synthesis aims to synthesize novel-view videos from reference observations along user-defined camera trajectories. Maintaining global scene consistency throughout this process remains challenging for camera-conditioned interactive video generators. Existing approaches typically select reference frames based solely on camera poses, overlooking whether the content remains semantically relevant or even visible. To address these limitations, we draw inspiration from semantic and episodic memory in human cognition, in which semantic memory captures generalized knowledge across experiences, whereas episodic memory preserves information tied to specific past events and contexts. Motivated by the complementary roles of semantic and episodic memory, we introduce SE-Mem, a Semantic-Episodic Memory framework that organizes historical observations in a structured 3D representation and augments its elements with semantic importance scores. A two-stage memory retrieval strategy is designed to identify the most informative frames to provide contextual guidance. Taking into account both semantic significance and geometric visibility, SE-Mem preserves semantic coherence and fine-grained visual details during novel view synthesis. Extensive evaluations show that our approach improves visual quality and achieves competitive geometric consistency across multiple benchmarks.

AI.tldr: SE-Mem is a semantic-episodic memory framework for scene-consistent generative view synthesis that stores past observations in a structured 3D representation with semantic importance scores. It reports improved visual quality and competitive geometric consistency across several benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Camera-conditioned interactive video generators select reference frames by pose alone, which ignores whether the content is semantically relevant or visible, and so global scene consistency is hard to maintain.
AI.method: Inspired by semantic and episodic memory in human cognition, historical observations are organized in a 3D representation with semantic importance scores. A two-stage retrieval strategy selects the most informative frames, considering both semantic significance and geometric visibility.
AI.result: The abstract reports that the approach improves visual quality and achieves competitive geometric consistency across multiple benchmarks, without specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Retrieval that jointly weighs semantic importance and geometric visibility is presented as a way to preserve semantic coherence and fine visual detail in novel view synthesis.

title: Smooth bounding box for object detection
summary: Deep learning-based object detection models are highly dependent on the quality of annotated training data. However, large-scale datasets often contain inevitable label noise, with bounding box localization errors being a prevalent and impactful form in object detection. While label noise handling techniques are well-studied for image classification, their adaptation to the more complex problem of bounding box errors remains underexplored. To address this, we propose a novel Smooth Bounding Box (SBB) strategy to mitigate the adverse effects of bounding box annotation inaccuracies. Our key insight is that annotation errors are often linked to annotator factors rather than specific image content, allowing for a statistical correction approach. Based on object size distribution within datasets, we implement the SBB strategy through two methods: 1) Global Scaling Correction (GSC), which applies a uniform scaling factor to estimate and correct a global average error; and 2) Interval Scaling Correction (ISC), which categorizes objects by size into intervals and estimates a dedicated correction factor for each, enabling more precise, fine-grained calibration. For efficient optimization of multiple parameters in ISC, we design a tailored model fine-tuning strategy. Furthermore, we introduce a Normalized Residual Fluctuation (NRF) metric to quantitatively assess the smoothing effect and training stability. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently enhances detection accuracy across various model architectures. Both GSC and ISC achieve significant performance improvements over strong baselines, including the latest YOLOv11n, without adding inference overhead. The codes are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Smooth Bounding Box (SBB), a statistical correction for systematic bounding box annotation errors in object detection training, with Global Scaling Correction and Interval Scaling Correction. It reports consistent accuracy gains over strong baselines, including YOLOv11n, without inference overhead.
AI.motivation: Bounding box localization errors are a prevalent form of label noise in detection, but noise-handling techniques from classification have not been adapted to them. The authors argue that annotation errors are linked to annotator factors rather than image content.
AI.method: GSC applies a uniform scaling factor to correct a global average error. ISC groups objects into size intervals and estimates a correction factor for each, with a tailored fine-tuning strategy for the multiple parameters. A Normalized Residual Fluctuation (NRF) metric measures smoothing effect and training stability.
AI.result: The abstract states that both GSC and ISC significantly improve over strong baselines, including YOLOv11n, across architectures and multiple benchmarks, without specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Size-based statistical correction of box annotation errors is presented as a low-cost way to improve detector accuracy with no added inference cost.

title: ROD-Dataset: A Pedestrian-Perspective Benchmark of Urban Obstacle Classes for YOLO-Based Detection
summary: Two groups of pedestrians face avoidable risk on the city sidewalk: people living with visual impairment, who reach an obstacle before anything warns them, and people walking with divided attention, who register a hazard late or not at all. A vision system can warn them only about obstacles it has learned to recognize, so its training data limits the protection it offers. No suitable training set exists: public benchmarks are recorded from vehicles, aerial platforms, or fixed rigs, general-purpose detectors omit the street furniture that causes trips, and pedestrian-focused collections are confined to single regions with incompatible class schemes. This paper introduces the Real-time Obstacle Detection (ROD) dataset: more than 24,000 images and 40,000 annotated obstacles across 25 classes, from vehicles and people to the stairs, manholes, traffic cones, and benches that general-purpose detectors overlook. Because street furniture differs between cities, ROD unifies twenty-nine public collections onto one taxonomy and adds eye-level imagery from two contrasting cities on two continents, Tehran and Toronto. Every label is human-verified, and each capture campaign is admitted only after a compact detector shows it can learn the class. Six lightweight YOLO detectors (nano and tiny variants) benchmarked on ROD all exceed 0.86 recall; YOLO12n attains the highest recall (0.889), YOLO26n the highest precision (0.925), and YOLOv9t the best mAP@0.50 (0.882) with the fewest parameters. Because the recall and mAP rankings disagree, selecting a model by mAP does not minimize missed obstacles, so per-class recall is reported for all 25 classes.

AI.tldr: ROD is a pedestrian-perspective benchmark of 24,000+ images and 40,000+ annotated urban obstacles across 25 classes, unified from 29 public collections with eye-level imagery from Tehran and Toronto. Six lightweight YOLO detectors all exceed 0.86 recall on it.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks come from vehicles, aerial platforms or fixed rigs, and general-purpose detectors omit street furniture that causes trips, so pedestrians with visual impairment or divided attention lack suitable training data for warnings.
AI.method: The dataset unifies 29 public collections onto one taxonomy and adds eye-level imagery from two cities on two continents. Every label is human-verified, and each capture campaign is admitted only after a compact detector shows it can learn the class.
AI.result: Six lightweight YOLO detectors (nano and tiny variants) all exceed 0.86 recall. YOLO12n has the highest recall (0.889), YOLO26n the highest precision (0.925), and YOLOv9t the best mAP@0.50 (0.882) with the fewest parameters. Per-class recall is reported for all 25 classes.
AI.conclusion: Recall and mAP rankings disagree, so selecting a model by mAP does not minimize missed obstacles, and per-class recall should be reported for pedestrian safety applications.

title: Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending for Training-Free Style Personalization
summary: Reference-based style personalization should reproduce the appearance of a style reference while preserving the subject specified by a content prompt. In visual autoregressive models, dominant reference features can also carry object and spatial information, causing content leakage. We propose Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending (CoPFB), a training-free method that estimates a low-rank content basis from a clean generation branch and removes the content-aligned component of the style residual. CoPFB applies rank-one blending at the first two autoregressive scales, followed by weaker content-projected refinement at the next three scales. On 1,900 combinations of Parti content prompts and FineStyle reference images, CoPFB improves text alignment from 0.293 to 0.297 and the harmonic score from 0.391 to 0.393 over PFB+SAC, while style similarity decreases from 0.590 to 0.577. CoPFB requires no fine-tuning or learnable parameters. Project page: this https URL.

AI.tldr: CoPFB is a training-free style personalization method for visual autoregressive models that removes the content-aligned part of the style residual to reduce content leakage. On 1,900 prompt-reference combinations it improves text alignment over PFB+SAC while reducing style similarity.
AI.motivation: In visual autoregressive models, dominant reference features can carry object and spatial information, causing content leakage when personalizing a style.
AI.method: A low-rank content basis is estimated from a clean generation branch, and the content-aligned component of the style residual is removed. Rank-one blending is applied at the first two autoregressive scales, followed by weaker content-projected refinement at the next three scales. No fine-tuning or learnable parameters are needed.
AI.result: Compared with PFB+SAC, text alignment rises from 0.293 to 0.297 and the harmonic score from 0.391 to 0.393, while style similarity falls from 0.590 to 0.577, on 1,900 combinations of Parti prompts and FineStyle references.
AI.conclusion: Projecting out the content component of the style residual trades a small loss in style similarity for better content preservation, without any training.

title: Density-Aware Calibration for Resource-Efficient Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for clinical image understanding, but their computational and memory requirements hinder deployment on resource-constrained clinical hardware. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical compression strategy without retraining, yet its effectiveness depends strongly on the calibration data. We propose CoreCalib, a training-free and quantizer-agnostic framework for constructing compact calibration sets that preserve the target medical VQA distribution. CoreCalib stratifies data by clinical question class, identifies representative visual modes using frozen DINOv2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN, and expands selected images into class-balanced question-answer pairs. On Kvasir-VQA-x1, we evaluate CoreCalib with MASQuant, GPTQ, and QIG using a fixed 128-pair budget. CoreCalib achieves the best METEOR with all three quantizers and the best ROUGE-L with MASQuant and GPTQ. With W4A8 MASQuant, it improves METEOR from 0.5672 with COCO calibration to 0.6234, recovering approximately 41% of the degradation relative to BF16. These results support CoreCalib as a data-centric component for resource-efficient medical VLM deployment. Project page: this https URL .

AI.tldr: CoreCalib builds compact, training-free calibration sets for post-training quantization of medical vision-language models by selecting representative visual modes per question class. With a 128-pair budget it recovers about 41% of the W4A8 METEOR degradation relative to BF16 on Kvasir-VQA-x1.
AI.motivation: Post-training quantization of medical VLMs depends strongly on calibration data, and generic calibration sets do not match the target medical VQA distribution.
AI.method: Data is stratified by clinical question class, representative visual modes are identified with frozen DINOv2 features, UMAP and HDBSCAN, and selected images are expanded into class-balanced question-answer pairs. The method is quantizer-agnostic and was tested with MASQuant, GPTQ and QIG.
AI.result: With W4A8 MASQuant, METEOR improves from 0.5672 with COCO calibration to 0.6234, recovering about 41% of the degradation relative to BF16. CoreCalib gives the best METEOR with all three quantizers and the best ROUGE-L with MASQuant and GPTQ.
AI.conclusion: Task-aware calibration data construction is presented as a practical, data-centric component for resource-efficient deployment of medical VLMs.

title: LoD-Loc v4: Towards Generalized Aerial Visual Localization via Panoptic LoD 3D Map Registration
summary: Aerial visual localization over Level-of-Detail (LoD) 3D Maps has recently gained significant traction due to its global scalability, storage efficiency, and privacy-preserving nature. However, existing methods rely almost exclusively on building elements, which leads to catastrophic localization failures in rural or undeveloped areas where buildings are sparse or non-existent. To address this, we construct a unified Panoptic LoD 3D Map by fusing OpenStreetMap (OSM), Digital Elevation Models (DEM), and LoD assets, reformulating the problem as a panoptic registration task. By parsing the query image into discrete building `thing' instances and continuous `stuff' regions comprising road, vegetation, and water, we establish a holistic alignment with this map to robustly optimize the camera pose. To enable reliable panoptic perception, we develop a new automated pipeline that constructs AirPan - the largest aerial panoptic segmentation dataset to date, comprising 85k images with pixel-accurate annotations. This empowers our panoptic segmentation model to exhibit remarkable zero-shot generalization capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LoD-Loc v4 consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines by a significant margin. Most notably, it successfully maintains reliable localization in building-less scenarios, completely overcoming the catastrophic failures of prior building-centric paradigms.

AI.tldr: LoD-Loc v4 localizes aerial images against a panoptic LoD 3D map that fuses OpenStreetMap, DEM and LoD assets, registering both building and stuff regions such as roads, vegetation and water. It stays reliable in building-less areas where building-centric methods fail.
AI.motivation: Aerial visual localization over LoD 3D maps depends almost entirely on building elements, which causes catastrophic failures in rural or undeveloped areas where buildings are sparse or absent.
AI.method: A unified Panoptic LoD 3D Map is built from OSM, DEM and LoD assets, and the task is cast as panoptic registration. The query image is parsed into building thing instances and stuff regions, and the camera pose is optimized against the map. A new pipeline builds AirPan, an aerial panoptic segmentation dataset of 85k pixel-accurate images.
AI.result: The abstract reports that LoD-Loc v4 consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by a significant margin and maintains reliable localization in building-less scenes. No specific numbers are given.
AI.conclusion: Holistic panoptic alignment with the map removes the failure mode of building-centric localization, and the AirPan dataset supports zero-shot generalization of the segmentation model.

title: Adversarial robustness does not entail human-aligned categorization
summary: Adversarial training can improve some forms of correspondence between artificial and biological vision, but whether robust classifiers acquire human-aligned classification behavior remains unclear. We generated 1,008 controversial stimuli by optimizing latent inputs to a pretrained GAN to elicit high-confidence disagreements between pairs of robust ImageNet classifiers. We compared four adversarially robust ImageNet classifiers - ResNet-101, ViT-B, ConvNeXt-L, and Swin-L - with two-alternative category judgments from 60 participants. We first evaluated each classifier on stimuli optimized to elicit disagreement with another model. Across classifiers, accuracy in predicting individual participants' single-trial category choices was near chance (48.6-51.3%), whereas majority judgments from other participants predicted responses with 85.0-86.8% accuracy. An analysis incorporating model prediction strength and participants' reported confidence found weak positive model-human correspondence for the two convolutional models. On stimuli optimized for disagreement between other model pairs, all four robust classifiers predicted human responses above chance but less accurately than predictions based on other participants' majority judgments; the same pattern held for 17 additional RobustBench models not used in stimulus generation. Across these 17 models, mean model-participant agreement was 67.3%, versus 81.3% mean participant-participant agreement on the same images. These results identify model-specific failures of human alignment and a model-human mismatch that persists across robust classifiers and substantially exceeds disagreement among human observers. Our findings show that adversarial robustness alone does not guarantee human-aligned categorization and suggest that robustness and human alignment should be evaluated as distinct properties of visual recognition systems.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that adversarially robust ImageNet classifiers do not reliably match human categorization. Using 1,008 controversial GAN stimuli, robust models predict individual human choices near chance, while human majority judgments predict them far better.
AI.motivation: Adversarial training can improve some correspondences between artificial and biological vision, but whether robust classifiers acquire human-aligned classification behavior was unclear.
AI.method: Controversial stimuli were generated by optimizing latent GAN inputs to elicit high-confidence disagreements between pairs of robust classifiers. Four robust ImageNet classifiers (ResNet-101, ViT-B, ConvNeXt-L, Swin-L) were compared with two-alternative judgments from 60 participants, with additional evaluation on 17 RobustBench models.
AI.result: Single-trial prediction accuracy of individual choices is 48.6-51.3%, near chance, while other participants' majority judgments predict responses with 85.0-86.8% accuracy. Across 17 additional models, mean model-participant agreement is 67.3%, against 81.3% mean participant-participant agreement.
AI.conclusion: Adversarial robustness alone does not guarantee human-aligned categorization, and robustness and human alignment should be evaluated as distinct properties of recognition systems.

title: SAVIER: Source-Anchored Visual Inspection and Evidence-Guided Repair for Vietnamese Cultural Text-to-Image Generation
summary: We present SAVIER, a training-free, one-pass framework that repairs the depiction of a named Vietnamese cultural entity in a generated image while preserving the scene details requested by the user. The problem is hard because a plausible scene can miss the cues that identify the entity, and prompt-level refinement never inspects the image it produces. SAVIER starts from a Culture-TRIP expanded prompt; a Curator separates source-linked cultural cues from prompt-preservation requirements, a prompt-blind Observer describes the first image, and a Refiner turns the discrepancies into at most three positive instructions before one regeneration with the same seed and a fixed bank of reference photographs. On the 50 bilingual prompts of ViCuP, evaluated with SDXL and FLUX.1-dev against a frozen, human-verified visual contract, SAVIER raises contract fulfillment from 55.6 to 69.6 and from 59.1 to 67.3 over Culture-TRIP and raises CAIRE cultural relevance on FLUX.1-dev. A reference-only ablation that removes the agent repair shows that SAVIER's photographs account for most of the contract gain; the agent roles add country-level relevance on FLUX.1-dev without lowering adherence to the original prompt under the official VQAScore. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: SAVIER is a training-free, one-pass pipeline that repairs the depiction of a named Vietnamese cultural entity in a text-to-image output while keeping the requested scene. It raises contract fulfillment on ViCuP from 55.6 to 69.6 with SDXL and from 59.1 to 67.3 with FLUX.1-dev, relative to Culture-TRIP.
AI.motivation: A plausible generated scene may lack the visual cues that identify a cultural entity, and prompt-level refinement never inspects the image actually produced.
AI.method: Starting from a Culture-TRIP expanded prompt, a Curator separates source-linked cultural cues from preservation requirements, a prompt-blind Observer describes the first image, and a Refiner turns discrepancies into at most three positive instructions. The image is then regenerated with the same seed and a fixed bank of reference photographs.
AI.result: On the 50 bilingual ViCuP prompts, contract fulfillment rises from 55.6 to 69.6 (SDXL) and from 59.1 to 67.3 (FLUX.1-dev) over Culture-TRIP. CAIRE cultural relevance improves on FLUX.1-dev. A reference-only ablation attributes most of the contract gain to the photographs, and the agent roles add country-level relevance without lowering VQAScore adherence.
AI.conclusion: Reference photographs supply most of the gain, and the inspect-and-repair agent roles add cultural relevance without hurting adherence to the original prompt.

title: SceneBound: How Much Should a Streaming 3D Reconstruction Model Remember?
summary: Streaming 3D reconstruction models keep past video frames in a recurrent state, fast weights from test-time training, or a key-value (KV) cache. Each written frame shifts the coordinate frame of later cameras or occupies GPU memory. Training-free rules decide what to write from a signal of the current frame. How much they write accounts for their mean accuracy: spending the update budget of a gate at uniformly spaced frames, with no signal, matches nine published gates, and the budget bounds the drift of the state wherever the writes fall. We propose SceneBound, a training-free rule that writes a frame only when its predicted camera pose lies at least a fixed radius from every stored keyframe. Its keyframe count stays within a constant factor of the covering number of the visited poses, the fewest views that keep a keyframe near every camera, so the count grows with the places visited and stays flat when the camera returns. In large scenes, SceneBound closes a submap once decoding its first frame again reveals drift. SceneBound uses one radius across four released models and three memory types. In the recurrent state of CUT3R and the KV cache of StreamVGGT, it achieves the lowest mean trajectory error among the published training-free rules we evaluate, in one pass and over nine passes of a scene, where its keyframes grow by 3% to 6%.

AI.tldr: SceneBound is a training-free rule for streaming 3D reconstruction models that writes a frame to memory only when its predicted camera pose is at least a fixed radius from every stored keyframe. It gives the lowest mean trajectory error among published training-free rules, with keyframe growth of 3% to 6%.
AI.motivation: Streaming reconstruction models keep past frames in a recurrent state, fast weights or a KV cache, and each write shifts later coordinate frames or uses GPU memory. The write budget, rather than the write signal, largely explains the accuracy of existing gates.
AI.method: A frame is stored only when its predicted pose is at least one fixed radius from all keyframes, so the keyframe count stays within a constant factor of the covering number of visited poses. A submap is closed when decoding the first frame again reveals drift. One radius is used across four released models and three memory types.
AI.result: In the recurrent state of CUT3R and the KV cache of StreamVGGT, SceneBound achieves the lowest mean trajectory error among the published training-free rules evaluated, in one pass and over nine passes of a scene, with keyframes growing by 3% to 6%. Uniformly spaced writes with no signal match nine published gates.
AI.conclusion: Bounding the write budget by pose coverage gives a simple, training-free memory policy whose keyframe count grows with the places visited rather than with time.

title: Old Is Not False: Valid-Time Memory for Interactive Video World Models
summary: Interactive video world models draw each frame from a memory bank of earlier frames stamped with their capture times. With frames, weights and noise fixed, reversing the timestamps of two views flips the state that generators of two families draw: they take the newest timestamp as the truth. That reading is right as long as states never return. After an agent undoes an action, the newest view of a region is outdated and the only view of the present is older; memories for changing worlds delete that older view, and memories that keep it hand the generator the past. Temporal databases separate when a record is stored from when its content holds, its valid time. ReDate keeps every frame and dates each retrieved token by its valid time, read from the agent's action log. The frozen generator then reads a reverted region as one that has just reached a new state, so ReDate needs no training. We prove that trusting the newest timestamp is right exactly when every current view is dated after every outdated one, that without a view taken after the return only the action log tells a reverted region from an up-to-date one, and that a generator able to draw from its own prediction gains more from re-dating than from deletion when the moved tokens keep little weight. After an undo, ReDate raises the share of FAR's steps showing the current state from 0.36 to 0.62 and HY-WorldPlay's from 0.003 to 0.19. We also propose a calibrated state metric to test any memory after undos.

AI.tldr: ReDate is a training-free method for interactive video world models that dates each retrieved memory token by its valid time, read from the agent's action log, so that reverted regions are not treated as the newest state. After an undo it raises the share of steps showing the current state from 0.36 to 0.62 for FAR.
AI.motivation: Memory banks stamped with capture times treat the newest timestamp as the truth, which fails after an agent undoes an action, because the newest view of a region is then outdated and the only view of the present is older.
AI.method: ReDate keeps every frame and dates retrieved tokens by valid time, drawn from the agent's action log, rather than by storage time. The frozen generator then reads a reverted region as having just reached a new state, so no training is needed. The authors prove when trusting the newest timestamp is correct and when re-dating outperforms deletion.
AI.result: After an undo, the share of FAR's steps showing the current state rises from 0.36 to 0.62, and HY-WorldPlay's rises from 0.003 to 0.19. A calibrated state metric for testing memories after undos is also proposed.
AI.conclusion: Separating storage time from valid time makes interactive world-model memory correct after reversals, and the work supplies both a method and a test metric.

title: DADKC: Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation for Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification
summary: Lifelong Person Re-identification (LReID) aims to match the same person using sequentially collected data. In practical long-term deployments, however, the model must handle both domain shifts across cameras and scenes, and irregular clothing changes of the same identity. This gives rise to the Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification (CH-LReID) task, which demands balancing cloth-relevant and cloth-irrelevant knowledge in streaming data. While existing LReID methods have explored replay-based or distillation-based anti-forgetting strategies, they typically fail to sufficiently model stage-aware domain distributions and cross-stage feature continuity under exemplar-free training. To address this problem, we propose a Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DADKC) framework. The core idea is to enhance the existing Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DKC) paradigm with adaptive distribution modeling. To this end, three lightweight modules are designed: (1) an Anchor Pool Adapter (APA) to retrieve learnable anchor cues for refining identity features; (2) a Phase Path Mixer (PPM) to perform stage-aware expert routing for integrating domain-specific distribution paths; and (3) a Stage Bridge Alignment (SBA) module to regularize the continuity of base, anchor, and path representations between adjacent stages. Extensive experiments on the CH-LReID and LReID benchmarks show that DADKC gains 4.1%/4.5% mAP/R1 on Order-1 and 3.6%/3.4% mAP/R1 on Order-2 over the DKC baseline, and lowers weighted forgetting from 2.4%/1.7% to 1.8%/1.4%, while storing neither historical images nor per-image features. The code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: DADKC extends Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation for cloth-hybrid lifelong person re-identification, where clothing changes occur alongside domain shifts. It adds three lightweight modules and gains 4.1%/4.5% mAP/R1 over the DKC baseline on Order-1, without storing historical images or features.
AI.motivation: Lifelong re-ID must handle camera and scene domain shifts as well as irregular clothing changes, and existing replay or distillation methods do not model stage-aware domain distributions or cross-stage feature continuity under exemplar-free training.
AI.method: Three modules are added: an Anchor Pool Adapter (APA) that retrieves learnable anchor cues to refine identity features, a Phase Path Mixer (PPM) that routes stage-aware experts across domain-specific distribution paths, and a Stage Bridge Alignment (SBA) module that regularizes continuity between adjacent stages.
AI.result: On CH-LReID and LReID benchmarks, DADKC gains 4.1%/4.5% mAP/R1 on Order-1 and 3.6%/3.4% mAP/R1 on Order-2 over the DKC baseline, and reduces weighted forgetting from 2.4%/1.7% to 1.8%/1.4%.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive distribution modeling within a differentiated consolidation framework reduces forgetting and improves accuracy without storing historical images or per-image features.

title: DramaVQA: Probing Detailed Understanding of Ultra-Long TV Dramas
comment: 36 pages. Project page: this https URL
summary: Despite recent progress in long-form video understanding, current benchmarks mostly focus on short clips or hour-scale videos. This leaves a major gap in evaluating ultra-long video understanding, where videos often last tens of hours. To bridge this gap, we introduce DramaVQA, a large-scale benchmark built upon long-form TV dramas. Containing approximately 20K question-answering (QA) pairs, the scale of DramaVQA exceeds previous long-video datasets, such as Video-MME and LVBench, by an order of magnitude. Our benchmark has two main features that make it stand out from existing datasets. First, we establish a scalable, LLM-assisted annotation pipeline that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate complex questions, followed by strict human checking to ensure high data quality. Second, DramaVQA introduces a multi-level time structure; queries are designed across different video lengths, with the hardest questions requiring overall understanding across the entire drama. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art MLLMs face major challenges when tested on these very long videos, highlighting the need for agentic AI algorithms capable of managing long-term memory. The project is available at this https URL

AI.tldr: DramaVQA is a benchmark of about 20K question-answer pairs over ultra-long TV dramas, with a multi-level time structure and questions that span from short segments to the whole drama. State-of-the-art MLLMs face major challenges on it.
AI.motivation: Existing long-video benchmarks focus on short clips or hour-scale videos, leaving ultra-long videos of tens of hours without suitable evaluation.
AI.method: An LLM-assisted pipeline uses multimodal LLMs to generate complex questions, followed by strict human checking. Queries are designed across different video lengths, and the hardest require understanding the entire drama.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art MLLMs struggle on these very long videos. The abstract gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Ultra-long video understanding needs agentic methods that can manage long-term memory, and DramaVQA is provided as a benchmark for probing this.

title: Now You See Them, Now You Dont FusionGhost Gait for Occlusion-Robust Gait Recognition with ArabGait dataset
comment: Submitted to "Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence", Elsevier
summary: Skeleton-based gait recognition is generally more robust to appearance changes than pixel-based methods, but this robustness depends on stable pose extraction. Clothing variation in gait recognition includes changes in garments, silhouette, and carried items; under Gulf clothing (Kandoora/Abaya), the dominant failure mode shifts from appearance change to lower-limb pose degradation caused by severe occlusion. To study this regime, we introduce ArabGait, a 45-subject indoor multi-view dataset with four walking conditions across three viewpoints, and show that Gulf clothing lowers mean lower-limb confidence from 0.811 to 0.683 and raises lower-limb failure rate from 7.98% to 17.82%, with ankles most affected. We propose FusionGhost-Gait, a fused spatiotemporal architecture that integrates spatial graph blocks and temporal modeling in one residual unit, removes redundant channel projections, and uses compact temporal Ghost kernels as a lightweight regularization mechanism for pose-noisy trajectories while preserving efficient temporal downsampling. On ArabGait cross-clothing evaluation, including Protocol A and Protocol B, FusionGhost-Gait reaches up to 67.91% Rank-1 while remaining compact (108,970- 133,674 parameters and 0.035-0.052 billion floating-point operations (GFLOPs)), achieving more than 65% fewer parameters and 75% lower FLOPs than existing baselines. These results indicate that the proposed model generalizes effectively to challenging Gulf-clothing conditions while remaining lightweight and deployable for surveillance and access-control biometric systems.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces ArabGait, a 45-subject multi-view gait dataset with Gulf clothing, and FusionGhost-Gait, a lightweight skeleton-based model that reaches up to 67.91% Rank-1 on cross-clothing evaluation with 108,970-133,674 parameters.
AI.motivation: Under Gulf clothing (Kandoora and Abaya), the dominant failure in skeleton-based gait recognition shifts to lower-limb pose degradation caused by occlusion. Clothing lowers mean lower-limb confidence from 0.811 to 0.683, and raises lower-limb failure rate from 7.98% to 17.82%, with ankles most affected.
AI.method: FusionGhost-Gait fuses spatial graph blocks and temporal modeling in one residual unit, removes redundant channel projections, and uses compact temporal Ghost kernels as lightweight regularization for pose-noisy trajectories while keeping efficient temporal downsampling.
AI.result: On ArabGait cross-clothing evaluation under Protocols A and B, the model reaches up to 67.91% Rank-1, with 65% fewer parameters and 75% lower FLOPs than existing baselines, at 0.035-0.052 GFLOPs.
AI.conclusion: The model generalizes to Gulf-clothing conditions while staying compact enough for surveillance and access-control biometric deployment.

title: FB-MOAC: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are effective in solving problems that can be modeled as Markov decision processes (MDPs). These algorithms primarily target forward MDPs whose dynamics evolve over time from an initial state. However, several important problems in different scenarios including stochastic control and network systems exhibit both a forward and a backward dynamics. As a consequence, they cannot be expressed as a standard MDP, thereby calling for a novel theory for RL in this context. Accordingly, this work introduces the concept of Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes (FB-MDPs) for multi-objective problems, develops a novel theoretical framework to characterize their optimal solutions, and proposes a general forward-backward step-wise template that allows to adapt RL algorithms for FB-MDP problems. A Forward Backward Multi Objective Actor Critic (FB-MOAC) algorithm is introduced accordingly to obtain optimal policies with guaranteed convergence and a competitive rate with respect to standard approaches in RL. FB-MOAC is evaluated on diverse use cases in the context of mathematical finance and mobile resource management. The obtained results show that FB-MOAC outperforms the state of the art across different metrics, highlighting its ability to learn and maximize rewards.

AI.tldr: FB-MOAC is a reinforcement learning algorithm for Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes, a new framework for multi-objective problems with both forward and backward dynamics. It reports better results than the state of the art on finance and mobile resource management use cases.
AI.motivation: Standard RL targets forward MDPs that evolve from an initial state, but problems in stochastic control and network systems have both forward and backward dynamics and cannot be written as standard MDPs.
AI.method: FB-MDPs are introduced with a theoretical framework for their optimal solutions and a general forward-backward step-wise template for adapting RL algorithms. The Forward Backward Multi Objective Actor Critic (FB-MOAC) instantiates this template.
AI.result: FB-MOAC is evaluated on use cases in mathematical finance and mobile resource management and is reported to outperform the state of the art across different metrics, with guaranteed convergence and a competitive rate compared with standard RL approaches.
AI.conclusion: Adapting actor-critic methods to forward-backward dynamics is presented as a principled extension of RL beyond standard MDPs.

title: Interpretable structural temperature scaling for calibrating graph neural networks and point-cloud segmentation
comment: Under consideration at Pattern Recognition Letters. 7 pages, 6 tables, 1 figure; supplementary material in ancillary files
summary: Graph-aware calibrators make graph neural networks (GNNs) more trustworthy by predicting a temperature for each node, usually with auxiliary networks whose decisions are hard to inspect. We propose Interpretable Structural Temperature Scaling (ISTS), a twelve-parameter linear model that sets each node's temperature from named descriptors of its confidence, neighbourhood and closeness to labelled nodes, so every temperature traces back to descriptor contributions. ISTS preserves predictions, and cross-validated regularisation lets the calibration data decide how far the model departs from temperature scaling (TS). Its explanations are faithful at the level of node groups: on test nodes, ISTS softens groups that a global temperature leaves over-confident and sharpens under-confident ones (Spearman correlation 0.67 over 246 groups). On seven graphs with two backbones and eleven baselines, ISTS has the best average rank in negative log-likelihood (NLL) and Brier score and lowers NLL relative to TS by 1.8%, more than twice the gain of an identically fitted entropy-based temperature. It ranked first again on four held-out graphs under a protocol fixed in advance. From about 100 calibration nodes on, ISTS is a cheap and inspectable choice, and on point-cloud segmentation it significantly improves NLL, Brier score and the ranking of points for rejection.

AI.tldr: ISTS is a twelve-parameter linear model that calibrates graph neural networks by setting each node's temperature from named, inspectable descriptors of confidence, neighbourhood and closeness to labelled nodes. It has the best average rank in NLL and Brier score across seven graphs.
AI.motivation: Graph-aware calibrators predict per-node temperatures with auxiliary networks whose decisions are hard to inspect, so their outputs are difficult to explain.
AI.method: Each node's temperature is a linear function of named descriptors of its confidence, neighbourhood and closeness to labelled nodes. Cross-validated regularization decides how far the model departs from global temperature scaling (TS), and predictions are preserved.
AI.result: Across seven graphs with two backbones and eleven baselines, ISTS has the best average rank in NLL and Brier score and lowers NLL relative to TS by 1.8%, more than twice the gain of an identically fitted entropy-based temperature. It ranks first again on four held-out graphs under a pre-fixed protocol, and it improves NLL, Brier score and rejection ranking on point-cloud segmentation. Group-level explanations correlate with over-confidence (Spearman 0.67 over 246 groups).
AI.conclusion: From about 100 calibration nodes onward, ISTS is presented as a cheap and inspectable alternative to auxiliary-network calibrators.

title: IsoAlign: Isoform-Aware DNA-Protein Alignment via Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
summary: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning DNA sequence representations, yet existing self-supervised pretraining strategies overlook alternative splicing and underperform compared to specialized models. To address this gap, we introduce IsoAlign, a multimodal framework that grounds genomic pretraining in isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment to learn biologically meaningful representations. IsoAlign aligns transcripts to their corresponding protein isoforms, capturing both coding sequences and broader regulatory contexts, using two Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA): DNA-Protein JEPA (DP-JEPA), which predicts protein representations from DNA using contrastive alignment, and Isoform-Masked JEPA (IM-JEPA), which models relationships among alternative isoforms of the same gene through masked protein prediction. We evaluate the learned DNA representations of these architectures across a multi-metric evaluation suite spanning tasks, including the prediction of pathogenicity, fitness, gene expression, and TF binding. Our results demonstrate that isoform-aware cross-modal alignment using JEPA significantly improves functional representations and downstream performance, establishing a promising direction for GFM pretraining.

AI.tldr: IsoAlign is a multimodal genomic pretraining framework that aligns DNA transcripts with their protein isoforms using two Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures. It reports that isoform-aware cross-modal alignment improves DNA representations on pathogenicity, fitness, expression and TF-binding tasks.
AI.motivation: Genomic foundation models use self-supervised pretraining that overlooks alternative splicing and underperform specialized models.
AI.method: DNA-Protein JEPA (DP-JEPA) predicts protein representations from DNA with contrastive alignment. Isoform-Masked JEPA (IM-JEPA) models relationships among alternative isoforms of the same gene through masked protein prediction. Transcripts are aligned with their corresponding protein isoforms, covering coding sequences and broader regulatory context.
AI.result: The abstract reports that the learned representations improve functional representations and downstream performance across a multi-metric suite covering pathogenicity, fitness, gene expression and TF binding, without specific numbers.
